# turkishcoffee — guide for AI agents

React 19 component library: Tailwind v4, Base UI primitives, `cva` variants, `cn()`
class merging, ESM-only. It is **shaped like shadcn/ui but it is not shadcn**: it
is an installed package (not copied source), and a few APIs differ. Read the
"Differences from shadcn/ui" section before writing code; most mistakes come
from assuming shadcn's API.

Per-component docs: `docs/<component>.md` next to this file
(`node_modules/turkishcoffee/docs/` in an installed project). Every export also
carries JSDoc with an example — hover or go to definition.

## Setup

The package ships Tailwind class strings, not compiled CSS. The app's global
stylesheet (e.g. `app/globals.css`) must contain all three lines:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "turkishcoffee/theme.css";
@source "../node_modules/turkishcoffee/dist";
```

- **`@source` is required.** Without it every component renders unstyled, with
  no error or warning. If components look unstyled, check this line first.
- The `@source` path is relative to the CSS file. In pnpm or monorepos
  `node_modules` may be symlinked; point it at the real path if styles are missing.
- Peers: `react@^19`, `react-dom@^19`, `tailwindcss@^4`. Do not install
  `tailwindcss-animate`, `tw-animate-css`, `lucide-react` or `sonner` for this
  library — it needs none of them.
- Dark mode is class-based: `<html class="dark">`.
- Wrap the app in an element with `isolation: isolate` (e.g. `<div className="isolate">`
  inside `<body>`). Popups render in portals; the separate stacking context keeps
  them above the page whatever `z-index` the page uses.

## Imports

| What | Import from |
|---|---|
| All components, `cn`, `useDisclosure`, `useMediaQuery`, `toast` | `turkishcoffee` |
| `Form`, `FormField`, `FormItem`, `FormLabel`, `FormControl`, `FormDescription`, `FormMessage`, `FormErrorSummary`, `useFormField`, `FormTabs`, `FormTabsList`, `FormTabsTrigger`, `FormTabsContent`, `FormTabsNext`, `FormTabsPrevious`, `useFormTabs` | `turkishcoffee/form` (needs `react-hook-form`) |
| `DataTable`, `DataTableColumn`, `dataTableFeatures`, `actionsColumn` | `turkishcoffee/data-table` (needs `@tanstack/react-table` v9) |
| Theme tokens | `turkishcoffee/theme.css` (CSS only) |

There are no per-component paths like `turkishcoffee/button` and no
`@/components/ui/*` files — never generate those imports.

## Differences from shadcn/ui

| shadcn habit | turkishcoffee |
|---|---|
| `<Button size="default">` | `size="md"` (sizes: `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `icon`; 32/36/40px). Variants: `primary` (default) · `secondary` (bordered) · `ghost` · `link` — no `default`, `outline`, `destructive` or `success`. |
| `toast("Saved")` / `toast.success("Saved")` (sonner) | Same sonner API, re-exported: `toast('Saved')`, `toast.success('Saved', { description })`, `toast.error`, `toast.info`, `toast.warning`. Import `toast` from `turkishcoffee`, not from `sonner`. |
| `<Toaster />` from `sonner`, or a `useToast()` hook | `import { Toaster, toast } from 'turkishcoffee'`; mount `<Toaster />` once at the app root. No `useToast`. |
| `<TooltipProvider>` around the app | Not needed and not exported: each `Tooltip` provides itself. |
| `import { Form } from '@/components/ui/form'` | `import { Form, … } from 'turkishcoffee/form'` — not from the root. |
| DataTable built by hand with `ColumnDef` / `createColumnHelper` (TanStack v8) | `import { DataTable, type DataTableColumn } from 'turkishcoffee/data-table'`; columns are `DataTableColumn<Row>[]` (TanStack v9). Interactions are opt-in props: `sortable`, `resizable` (double-click an edge to fit), `reorderable`, `hideable`, `selectable`, `selectableColumns`, `filterable`, `exportable`; `pageSize` paginates; `height` and `columnVirtualization` virtualize. A feature's options and state go in its own prop as an object in place of `true` (`selectable={{ value, onChange, scope, isRowSelectable, scopeKey }}`, `exportable={{ fetchRows | onServerExport, onError }}`, `layout={{ storageKey | saved, onChange, defaults }}`). Sorting, filters and page are one value: `query` + `onQueryChange(query, change)`, or `defaultQuery` — a sort on page 3 is one change, already on page 1, so never chain separate sort and page handlers. `ref` gives resets and `getExportData`. Column filters go in `meta.filter` (`variant`, `options`, `control`). A row's actions menu goes in `actionsColumn({ label, cell })`, not a hand-made column. Server data: `server={{ rowCount }}` — sorting, filtering and paging then happen on the server; `getRowId` is required with `selectable`. Name the grid with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. `locale` follows `LocaleProvider` (below), so a Turkish app passes nothing. |
| `lucide-react` icons inside components | Components draw their own icons. Pass any icon element where a `ReactNode` is accepted (`EmptyState icon`, inside `Button`). |
| `tailwindcss-animate` classes (`animate-in`, `fade-in-0`) | Overlays animate with CSS transitions on Base UI's `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`. There are no animation tokens; retime one with `className`, e.g. `duration-150`. |
| `asChild` (Radix) | `render`: `<Button render={<Link href="/x" />}>Go</Button>`, `<DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open</DialogTrigger>`. |
| `<Accordion type="single" collapsible>` | `<Accordion>` (one open at a time, closable) or `<Accordion multiple>`. `value` / `defaultValue` are arrays. |
| `<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={…}>` | `onClick={…}`. The menu closes afterwards. |
| `<SelectValue>` shows the item text | Pass `items` to `Select` (`{ value: label }` or `{ value, label }[]`); without it `SelectValue` shows the raw value. |
| `variant="destructive"` on Alert, Badge, DropdownMenuItem | Meaning is the `tone` prop: `neutral` · `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger`. `<Alert tone="danger">`, `<Badge tone="success">`, `<DropdownMenuItem tone="danger">`. `Button` has no tone. |
| Translating each component's strings by hand (`labels`, `placeholder`, `aria-label` copies) | Wrap the root in `<LocaleProvider locale="tr-TR">` (same locale as `<html lang>`): every word components render themselves — DataTable, pagination, filters, pickers, search, close buttons, spinners — comes out in that language, with its numerals and dates. English and Turkish ship complete; English is the fallback. Without a provider they follow `<html lang>` after hydration. Use `labels` only to change a single word, not to translate. |
| `<AlertDialogAction>` is plain | `AlertDialogAction` is styled as a primary Button and `AlertDialogCancel` as secondary. There is no destructive Button: keep the action primary and name the consequence in its label ("Delete project", not "OK"). |

## Upgrading from v2 (Radix) to v3 (Base UI)

| v2 | v3 |
|---|---|
| `asChild` + child element | `render={<Element />}`, children on the outer component |
| `<Accordion type="single" collapsible>` / `type="multiple"` | `<Accordion>` / `<Accordion multiple>`; `value` is always an array |
| `<Checkbox checked="indeterminate">` | `<Checkbox indeterminate>` |
| `<DropdownMenuItem onSelect>` | `onClick` |
| `<Tooltip delayDuration={…}>` | `delay={…}` |
| `<Select>` with `SelectValue` showing labels | add `items` to `Select` |
| `PopoverAnchor` | `anchor` prop on `PopoverContent` |
| `HoverCardTrigger asChild` around an `<a>` | `HoverCardTrigger` renders the `<a>`: give it `href` |
| `data-[state=open]` / `data-[state=checked]` / `data-[state=active]` selectors | `data-open` / `data-checked` / `data-active` (tabs) |
| `animate-ui-*` classes and `--animate-ui-*` tokens | removed; transitions on `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` |
| `Button`, `BreadcrumbLink` server-renderable | client components now (`render` needs a hook); `Label`, `Separator` and `AspectRatio` became server-renderable |

## Design language

turkishcoffee is built for data-dense business screens: fast, flat and sharp.
Every rule below is a token in `theme.css`; retune the token, not the components.

- **Corners are sharp.** `--radius` is 4px. `rounded-sm` (2px) for checkboxes,
  badges and list items; `rounded-md` (4px) for controls and popups;
  `rounded-lg` (6px) for cards, dialogs, sheets and toasts; `rounded-full` only
  for pills (switch, radio, avatar, progress). Never `rounded-[…]`.
- **Compact and aligned.** Controls use `h-control-sm` 32px · `h-control` 36px ·
  `h-control-lg` 40px (`--spacing-control*`). Button, Input, Select, NativeSelect,
  InputGroup and TabsList share them, so a form row lines up. Match them in your
  own controls instead of `h-9`.
- **Flat, with hairline borders.** Resting surfaces (buttons, inputs, cards)
  have no shadow; a 1px `border-border` separates them. `shadow-float` is the
  only elevation, reserved for layers that float: popovers, menus, dialogs,
  sheets, toasts. The app's frame draws no lines: the Sidebar has no edge,
  only its own faint grey (`bg-sidebar`), and a top bar beside it needs no
  bottom border.
- **No tint.** Highlighted and selected states use `bg-selection`, a neutral
  grey, never a primary tint or a coloured edge. An open accordion header looks
  like a closed one. One exception: the current page in a Sidebar takes a soft
  brand fill (`bg-primary-soft text-primary-text`) — it is where you are, not
  something you picked.
- **Fast.** Overlays enter and leave in 50ms. Don't slow them down per use.
- **Quiet colour.** Solid primary is for values, the main action and the
  active tab (checked checkbox, primary button, selected TabsTrigger); `--inverse` grey is for transient surfaces
  (toast, tooltip).

## Rules

- **Compose sub-parts**, don't look for props: `<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>`,
  not `<Card title="…">`. Every component's parts are listed in its doc.
- **`className` always wins.** Components merge with `cn()` (tailwind-merge), so
  `className="px-8"` overrides the built-in padding. Use `cn()` from
  `turkishcoffee` in your own components too.
- **Links:** pass `render` to `Button`, `BreadcrumbLink`, and the `*Trigger` /
  `*Close` parts: `<Button render={<Link href="/x" />}>Go</Button>`. The children
  stay on the outer component. `PaginationLink` takes `href` directly and does
  not support `render`.
- **Two props, two questions.** `tone` says what something means and is the
  same closed list everywhere: `neutral` · `info` · `success` · `warning` ·
  `danger` (Alert, Badge, DropdownMenuItem `neutral`/`danger`). `variant` says
  how loud it is: Button `primary` · `secondary` · `ghost` · `link`, Badge
  `soft` · `solid`. Never invent a new tone or variant name; compose the two.
- **Colours come from tokens**, never hex or the default palette:
  `bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-danger`,
  `text-success-text`, `bg-warning-soft`. Full list: `background`, `foreground`,
  `card`, `popover`, `primary`, `secondary`, `muted`, `accent`, `danger`,
  `success`, `warning`, `inverse` (each with `-foreground`), the soft tints
  `primary-soft`, `danger-soft`, `success-soft`, `warning-soft`, the readable
  text colours `primary-text`, `danger-text`, `success-text`, `warning-text`,
  plus `border`, `input`, `field`, `field-hover`, `ring`, `selection` and
  `sidebar`. `inverse` is the grey behind toasts and tooltips.
- **Coloured text and icons use the `-text` token, not the fill.**
  `primary`, `danger`, `success` and `warning` are fills (buttons, checked
  controls, solid badges); in dark mode a fill dark enough for white text is
  too dark to read as text, and the orange warning fill is under 3:1 on white.
  `text-primary-text`, `text-danger-text`, `text-success-text` and
  `text-warning-text` are at least 4.5:1 on the page and on their soft tint.
- **Fields** (Input, Textarea, Select, NativeSelect, InputGroup, DatePicker,
  Checkbox, RadioGroup) share one edge: `border-field`, `hover:border-field-hover`.
  A text field's focus stays inside its box: `focus-visible:border-ring
  focus-visible:inset-ring focus-visible:inset-ring-ring` (a 2px brand edge).
  Match it in your own fields. Bordered buttons keep the fainter `border-input`.
- **Focus** elsewhere is a solid 2px `ring-ring` (the readable brand blue);
  filled controls add `ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background` so it stays visible.
- **Server vs client:** components marked "Client component" in their doc ship
  `"use client"`. They can be imported from a server component as-is; your event
  handlers still need to live in a client component.
- **Dialog, AlertDialog and Sheet need their Title** (`DialogTitle`, …) for
  accessibility. Base UI event props apply, and every change handler gets a
  second `eventDetails` argument: `onOpenChange(open, eventDetails)`,
  `onCheckedChange`, `onValueChange`; menu items use `onClick`.
- **Choosing between look-alikes:**
  - Button (a form's or dialog's action) · CommandButton (borderless command in a toolbar; as a DropdownMenuTrigger it adds a chevron) · SplitButton (a main action plus a menu of related ones)
  - Dialog (centered task) · AlertDialog (confirm a consequential action) · Sheet (panel from an edge)
  - Popover (click, interactive) · Tooltip (hover, short text) · HoverCard (hover, rich preview)
  - Label · InfoLabel (label with an info button explaining the field; in a form, `<FormLabel info="…">`) — not a Tooltip on an icon, which touch users never see
  - Select (custom, client) · NativeSelect (platform picker, server-renderable, better on mobile) · Combobox (type to filter a long list — people, cities; `multiple` for chips)
  - Table (static markup, plus `TablePagination`, `TableCheckbox`, `TableColumnFilter`, `exportTable`) · DataTable (data grid: sort, filter, select rows/columns, resize, reorder, hide, export, virtualization, keyboard; client or server data)
  - Tabs (separate views) · FormTabs (one react-hook-form form split across tabs; `linear` for a stepper; use `FormTabsList`, not `TabsList`, inside it)
  - SegmentedControl (one of a few options that changes what a view shows, e.g. a list's status filter; one always pressed; counts with `SegmentedControlCount`) · Tabs (separate views with their own panels) · RadioGroup (a choice submitted with a form)
  - Checkbox (submitted with a form) · Switch (applies immediately)
  - Alert (inline, persistent) · `toast()` (transient)
  - Accordion (several sections) · Collapsible (one region) · Tree (a hierarchy people navigate: folders, an org chart; one tab stop, arrow keys)
  - Sidebar (the app's navigation; built on Tree) · Tabs (views inside one page) · Breadcrumb (where the page sits)
  - SearchField (search a list, debounced; `hideLabel` in toolbars, with `size="sm"` among 32px CommandButtons and the default `md` in DataTable's toolbar) · FileUpload (pick or drop files; the app uploads them)
  - Spinner (unknown duration) · Progress (known percentage) · Skeleton (content placeholder)
- **Hooks:** `useDisclosure()` returns `{ open, setOpen, onOpen, onClose, onToggle }`
  for controlled dialogs and sheets; `useMediaQuery('(min-width: 768px)')` is
  SSR-safe (false on the server).

## Components

<!-- components:start -->
- [Accordion](docs/accordion.md) · client — Vertically stacked sections.
- [Alert](docs/alert.md) · server — Inline, non-dismissable message inside the page flow (`role="alert"`).
- [AlertDialog](docs/alert-dialog.md) · client — Modal that interrupts the user to confirm a consequential action.
- [AspectRatio](docs/aspect-ratio.md) · server — Constrains its child (usually an image or video) to `ratio` (width / height) with the CSS `aspect-ratio` property.
- [Avatar](docs/avatar.md) · client — Round user image with a fallback while it loads or when it fails.
- [AvatarGroup](docs/avatar-group.md) · client — A stack of overlapping avatars for the people on a record.
- [Badge](docs/badge.md) · server — Small inline label for a status or count.
- [Breadcrumb](docs/breadcrumb.md) · client — Trail of links to the current page.
- [Button](docs/button.md) · client — A button.
- [Calendar](docs/calendar.md) · client — react-day-picker styled with the theme tokens instead of its stylesheet, so it follows `.dark`.
- [Card](docs/card.md) · server — Bordered surface that groups related content.
- [Checkbox](docs/checkbox.md) · client — A checkbox.
- [Collapsible](docs/collapsible.md) · client — A single region the user can show and hide.
- [Combobox](docs/combobox.md) · client — A text field that filters a list as you type, for picking one value (or several, with `multiple`) out of more than a Select comfortably holds: a manager out of 300 people, a city, a cost centre.
- [CommandButton](docs/command-button.md) · client — A borderless command for toolbars and command bars: text and icon neutral at rest; on hover a grey fill and the icon in the brand colour, as on a Button.
- [DataTable](docs/data-table.md) · client · `turkishcoffee/data-table` — A data grid over TanStack Table v9.
- [DatePicker](docs/date-picker.md) · client — Controlled single-date picker.
- [Dialog](docs/dialog.md) · client — Modal for a focused task (a form, details): centered on `sm` screens and up, a Base UI bottom drawer below.
- [Drawer](docs/drawer.md) · client — Bottom sheet built on Base UI's Drawer: slides up from the bottom edge and closes on a swipe down, outside tap or Escape.
- [DropdownMenu](docs/dropdown-menu.md) · client — Menu of actions opened from a trigger.
- [EmptyState](docs/empty-state.md) · server — Placeholder for a list or page that has no content yet: icon, title, description and a call to action.
- [FileUpload](docs/file-upload.md) · client — Picks files by drag-and-drop, click or keyboard and checks them against `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`.
- [Form](docs/form.md) · client · `turkishcoffee/form` — react-hook-form's FormProvider.
- [HoverCard](docs/hover-card.md) · client — Rich preview shown when a pointer hovers a link (e.g.
- [InfoLabel](docs/info-label.md) · client — A Label with an info button beside it that opens a short explanation.
- [Input](docs/input.md) · server — Single-line text field; a styled `<input>` that forwards every prop.
- [InputGroup](docs/input-group.md) · server — A field that combines a control with icons, text or buttons.
- [Label](docs/label.md) · server — Accessible label for a form control; link it with `htmlFor`.
- [LocaleProvider](docs/locale-provider.md) · client — The language and locale of every component below it: the words they render themselves (labels, screen-reader names, placeholders), and the formatting, sorting and dates that follow the locale.
- [NativeSelect](docs/native-select.md) · server — The platform <select>, styled to match Input.
- [Pagination](docs/pagination.md) · server — Page navigation built from plain anchors, so it works with any router: pass `href` to each link.
- [PasswordInput](docs/password-input.md) · client — A password field with a button that shows what was typed.
- [Popover](docs/popover.md) · client — Floating panel opened by clicking a trigger; for small forms, pickers and extra details.
- [Progress](docs/progress.md) · client — Horizontal bar for a known completion percentage (`value`, 0–100).
- [RadioGroup](docs/radio-group.md) · client — One choice out of a few visible options.
- [SearchField](docs/search-field.md) · client — A reusable search field with a label, debounce, clear button and loading indicator.
- [SegmentedControl](docs/segmented-control.md) · client — A row of mutually exclusive options that change what the page shows, such as a list's status filter: All · Active · Inactive.
- [Select](docs/select.md) · client — Custom-styled dropdown for picking one value.
- [Separator](docs/separator.md) · server — Thin horizontal or vertical (`orientation="vertical"`) rule.
- [Sheet](docs/sheet.md) · client — Modal panel that slides in from an edge — navigation drawers, filters, detail views.
- [Sidebar](docs/sidebar.md) · client — The app's side navigation: a header, the navigation itself (SidebarContent) and a footer.
- [Skeleton](docs/skeleton.md) · server — Placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading.
- [Spinner](docs/spinner.md) · client — Indeterminate loading indicator; `size-4`, inherits text colour.
- [SplitButton](docs/split-button.md) · client — A button with a main action and a menu of related ones: the left half runs the action, the chevron on the right opens the menu, which opens under the whole button from its left edge.
- [Switch](docs/switch.md) · client — On/off toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately.
- [Table](docs/table.md) · server — Plain styled table primitives — no data library, server-renderable; wraps the table in a horizontally scrolling container.
- [Tabs](docs/tabs.md) · client — Switches between views in the same place.
- [Textarea](docs/textarea.md) · server — Multi-line text field; grows with its content (`field-sizing-content`) from a minimum of `min-h-16`.
- [Toast](docs/toast.md) · client — Mount once, near the root of the app.
- [Tooltip](docs/tooltip.md) · client — Short text hint shown on hover and keyboard focus.
- [Tree](docs/tree.md) · client — A hierarchy people expand and collapse: folders and files, an org chart, nested categories, an app's navigation (Sidebar is built on it).

# Accordion

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Vertically stacked sections. One opens at a time and can be closed again;
pass `multiple` to let several stay open. `value` / `defaultValue` are always
arrays of item values. For a single show/hide region use Collapsible.

## Example

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue={['shipping']}>
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger>Shipping</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Ships in 2–3 days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Parts

- `AccordionItem` — One section of an Accordion. `value` must be unique within the Accordion.
- `AccordionTrigger` — The clickable heading of an AccordionItem; renders its own chevron.
- `AccordionContent` — The collapsible body of an AccordionItem. `className` lands on an inner padding wrapper, not on the animated element, so the height animation stays intact.

---

# Alert

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { alertVariants, Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, type AlertProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Inline, non-dismissable message inside the page flow (`role="alert"`).
`tone`: `neutral` (default) | `info` | `success` | `warning` | `danger`. Pass
an `icon` (or put an svg as the first child) and it gets its own column;
every tone but `neutral` brings its own. For a transient message use
`toast()`; for a blocking question use AlertDialog.

## Example

```tsx
<Alert tone="warning">
  <AlertTitle>Trial ends soon</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Add a payment method to keep your projects.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>

<Alert tone="info">
  <AlertTitle>Leave requests close on Friday</AlertTitle>
</Alert>
```

## Variants

| Prop | Options | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `tone` | `neutral` · `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | `"neutral"` |

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Icon in its own column before the text. Every tone but `neutral` brings one (InfoIcon, SuccessIcon, ErrorIcon for warning and danger); pass your own node to replace it, or `null` to drop it.

## Parts

- `alertVariants` — Alert classes as a function, for building alert-like elements.
- `type AlertProps`
- `AlertTitle` — Heading line of an Alert.
- `AlertDescription` — Body text of an Alert. Inherits the tone's colour at 80% rather than always going muted, so a danger alert stays readable as one block of colour.

---

# AlertDialog

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogPortal, AlertDialogOverlay, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialogCancel } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Modal that interrupts the user to confirm a consequential action. Unlike
Dialog it does not close on outside click; the user must pick Action or Cancel.
AlertDialogTitle is required for accessibility.

## Example

```tsx
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Delete project</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>This cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction onClick={remove}>Delete project</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>
```

## Parts

- `AlertDialogTrigger` — Opens the AlertDialog. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button the trigger.
- `AlertDialogPortal` — Portal used by AlertDialogContent. Rarely needed directly.
- `AlertDialogOverlay` — Backdrop behind the AlertDialog. Already rendered by AlertDialogContent.
- `AlertDialogContent` — The dialog panel. Renders its own portal and overlay.
- `AlertDialogHeader` — Stacks AlertDialogTitle and AlertDialogDescription.
- `AlertDialogFooter` — Holds AlertDialogCancel and AlertDialogAction; stacks on mobile, right-aligns from `sm`.
- `AlertDialogTitle` — Required: names the dialog for screen readers.
- `AlertDialogDescription` — Explains the consequence of the action.
- `AlertDialogAction` — The confirming button; closes the dialog after its `onClick`. Styled as a primary Button. Action and Cancel are pre-styled with buttonVariants: an alert dialog is a decision, so the two choices should never drift apart visually. A destructive action stays primary; its label names the consequence ("Delete project", not "OK").
- `AlertDialogCancel` — The dismissing button; closes the dialog. Styled as a secondary Button.

---

# AspectRatio

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { AspectRatio, type AspectRatioProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Constrains its child (usually an image or video) to `ratio` (width / height)
with the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. Server-renderable.

## Example

```tsx
<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}>
  <img src={src} alt="" className="size-full rounded-md object-cover" />
</AspectRatio>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `ratio?: number` — Width divided by height, e.g. `16 / 9`. Defaults to 1 (square).

## Parts

- `type AspectRatioProps`

---

# Avatar

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Round user image with a fallback while it loads or when it fails.
Defaults to `size-8`; resize with `className`. For several people, use AvatarGroup.

## Example

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage src={user.avatarUrl} alt={user.name} />
  <AvatarFallback>GK</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

## Parts

- `AvatarImage` — The image; hidden until it has loaded.
- `AvatarFallback` — Shown while AvatarImage loads or when it fails — usually initials.

---

# AvatarGroup

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupItem } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A stack of overlapping avatars for the people on a record. It spreads apart
on hover and keyboard focus. Shows `max` avatars (4 by default); the rest
collapse into a `+N` button that lists them by name. Children must be
AvatarGroupItems, passed directly (an array from `.map()` is fine). Give the
group an `aria-label` saying who they are.

## Example

```tsx
<AvatarGroup aria-label="Reviewers">
  {reviewers.map((r) => (
    <AvatarGroupItem key={r.id} name={r.name} src={r.avatarUrl} />
  ))}
</AvatarGroup>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `AvatarGroup`

- `max?: number` — How many avatars show before the rest collapse into `+N`.
- `size?: Size` — `sm` 28px · `md` 32px · `lg` 36px.
- `overflowLabel?: (count: number) => string` — Accessible name of the `+N` button.

### `AvatarGroupItem`

- `name: string` — The person's full name.
- `src?: string` — Image URL; initials show without one.
- `initials?: string` — Overrides the initials taken from `name`.
- `render?: React.ReactElement` — An element to render the avatar as, usually a link to the person.

## Parts

- `AvatarGroupItem` — One person in an AvatarGroup: their image, or their initials while it loads or when there is none. `name` is what screen readers announce, what the hover tooltip and the overflow list show. Pass `render` to make the avatar a link, e.g. to a profile: `render={<Link href="/people/42" />}`.

---

# Badge

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { badgeVariants, Badge, type BadgeProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Small inline label for a status or count. `tone` says what it means:
`neutral` (default) | `info` | `success` | `warning` | `danger`. `variant`
says how loud: `soft` (default, a tinted fill for statuses in tables and
lists) or `solid` (for counts and the one badge that must stand out). Not
interactive — wrap it in a Button or link if it needs to be clickable.

## Example

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Paid</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" variant="solid">3</Badge>
```

## Variants

| Prop | Options | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `tone` | `neutral` · `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | `neutral` |
| `variant` | `soft` · `solid` | `soft` |

## Parts

- `badgeVariants` — Badge classes as a function — style a link or other element like a Badge.
- `type BadgeProps`

---

# Breadcrumb

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbButton, BreadcrumbSeparator, BreadcrumbEllipsis, type BreadcrumbLinkProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Trail of links to the current page. The last item is a BreadcrumbPage,
not a link. A step's text truncates at about 30 characters and shows in full
in a tooltip; change the limit with `className="[--breadcrumb-text-max:50ch]"`.

## Example

```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/" />}>Home</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Parts

- `BreadcrumbList` — The ordered list holding BreadcrumbItems and BreadcrumbSeparators.
- `BreadcrumbItem` — One step of the trail.
- `type BreadcrumbLinkProps`
- `BreadcrumbLink` — A link to an ancestor page. Pass `render` to use your router's `<Link>`. Put an icon before the text as a child; it turns primary on hover.
- `BreadcrumbPage` — The current page. Not a link: it carries aria-current and is removed from the tab order, which is what screen readers expect at the end of a trail.
- `BreadcrumbButton` — A step that acts instead of navigating, styled like BreadcrumbLink. Use it as the trigger for a menu of collapsed steps: `<DropdownMenuTrigger render={<BreadcrumbButton aria-label="Show 3 more" />}><BreadcrumbEllipsis /></DropdownMenuTrigger>`.
- `BreadcrumbSeparator` — Goes between BreadcrumbItems; a chevron unless you pass children.
- `BreadcrumbEllipsis` — Stands in for collapsed middle steps of a long trail. Decorative: to let people reach those steps, put it inside a BreadcrumbButton that opens a menu.

---

# Button

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { buttonVariants, Button, type ButtonProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A button. Variants rank emphasis, not meaning: `primary` (default; one per
screen), `secondary` (bordered, for every other action), `ghost` (toolbars
and icon buttons) and `link` (inline in text). There is no coloured tone:
for a dangerous action say the consequence in the label ("Delete
employee") and confirm it in an AlertDialog. Sizes: `sm` (32px) | `md` (36px, default) |
`lg` (40px) | `icon` (36px square) | `icon-sm` (32px square, e.g. in a
`size="sm"` DataTable row) — from the `--spacing-control*` tokens; there is no
`size="default"`. Pass `render` to style another element, such
as your router's link, as a button. Client component.

## Example

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Export</Button>

<Button render={<Link href="/settings" />} variant="ghost">
  Settings
</Button>
```

## Variants

| Prop | Options | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `primary` · `secondary` · `ghost` · `link` | `"primary"` |
| `size` | `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `icon` · `"icon-sm"` | `"md"` |

## Parts

- `buttonVariants` — Button classes as a function — style a non-Button element (e.g. a Base UI trigger) like a Button.
- `type ButtonProps`

---

# Calendar

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Calendar, type DateRange, type CalendarProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

react-day-picker styled with the theme tokens instead of its stylesheet, so it
follows `.dark`. Month and day names, the week's first day and the
screen-reader labels follow LocaleProvider (else `<html lang>`); pass a
`locale` from `react-day-picker/locale` to choose another. Without `mode` it is a read-only month: mark days with `modifiers` and
style them with `modifiersClassNames`.

## Example

```tsx
<Calendar mode="single" selected={day} onSelect={setDay} />

<Calendar modifiers={{ holiday: holidays }} modifiersClassNames={{ holiday: 'text-danger-text' }} />
```

## Parts

- `type DateRange`
- `type CalendarProps`

---

# Card

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Bordered surface that groups related content. Server-renderable by design:
no state, no handlers, no "use client". Compose with the sub-parts rather than
passing title/footer props.

## Example

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Team</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Invite people to your workspace.</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>…</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="justify-end">
    <Button>Invite</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

## Parts

- `CardHeader` — Top section holding CardTitle and CardDescription.
- `CardTitle` — Card heading; renders an `<h3>`.
- `CardDescription` — Muted text under CardTitle.
- `CardContent` — Main body of the Card.
- `CardFooter` — Bottom row, usually actions. A flex row: align with `justify-*`.

---

# Checkbox

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Checkbox, type CheckboxProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A checkbox. Controlled with `checked` + `onCheckedChange` (not `onChange`);
the handler gets `(checked: boolean, eventDetails)`. Pass `indeterminate` for a
mixed state. Renders a native `<button>`, so pair it with a Label via
`id`/`htmlFor`. For an on/off setting that applies immediately, prefer Switch.

## Example

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <Checkbox id="terms" checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />
  <Label htmlFor="terms">Accept terms</Label>
</div>
```

## Parts

- `type CheckboxProps`

---

# Collapsible

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A single region the user can show and hide. For several related sections
use Accordion.

## Example

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" />}>
    Show details
  </CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>…</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

## Parts

- `CollapsibleTrigger` — Toggles the Collapsible. Unstyled — pass `render={<Button />}` to style it.
- `CollapsibleContent` — The region that shows and hides, with a height animation.

# Combobox

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxValue, ComboboxGroup, ComboboxCollection, useComboboxFilter, ComboboxInput, ComboboxChips, ComboboxChip, ComboboxChipsInput, ComboboxContent, ComboboxList, ComboboxItem, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxGroupLabel, ComboboxSeparator, type ComboboxInputProps, type ComboboxContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A text field that filters a list as you type, for picking one value (or
several, with `multiple`) out of more than a Select comfortably holds: a
manager out of 300 people, a city, a cost centre. Give it the options as
`items`; ComboboxList renders each through a function child and filters them
itself. For objects, pass `itemToStringLabel` so the input shows a label.
Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)`. For under a
dozen fixed options use Select.

## Example

```tsx
<Combobox items={people} itemToStringLabel={(p) => p.name} value={manager} onValueChange={setManager}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search people" aria-label="Manager" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No one matches.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(person: Person) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={person.id} value={person}>{person.name}</ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## More examples

### Several values, as chips

```tsx
<Combobox multiple items={skills} value={picked} onValueChange={setPicked}>
  <ComboboxChips>
    <ComboboxValue>
      {(values: string[]) => values.map((skill) => <ComboboxChip key={skill}>{skill}</ComboboxChip>)}
    </ComboboxValue>
    <ComboboxChipsInput placeholder="Add a skill" aria-label="Skills" />
  </ComboboxChips>
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxList>{(skill: string) => <ComboboxItem key={skill} value={skill}>{skill}</ComboboxItem>}</ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `ComboboxInputProps`

- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Height: `sm` (32px) or `md` (36px, default) — matches Button, Input and Select.
- `showClear?: boolean` — Show the × that clears the value once there is one. Defaults to true.
- `clearLabel?: string` — Accessible name of the clear button. Defaults to "Clear" in the page's language.
- `showTrigger?: boolean` — Show the chevron that opens the list without typing. Defaults to true.
- `triggerLabel?: string` — Accessible name of the chevron. Defaults to "Show options" in the page's language.
- `groupClassName?: string` — Classes on the field around the input (border, width). `className` styles the input.

### `ComboboxChip`

- `removeLabel?: string` — Accessible name of the × button. Defaults to "Remove" followed by the chip's text.

## Parts

- `ComboboxValue` — Renders the selected value(s) through a function child; use it inside ComboboxChips.
- `ComboboxGroup` — Groups ComboboxItems under a ComboboxGroupLabel.
- `ComboboxCollection` — Renders the items of a group passed as `{ value, items }` in `items`.
- `useComboboxFilter` — The default filter (locale-aware "contains"), for filtering `items` yourself.
- `type ComboboxInputProps`
- `ComboboxInput` — The single-value field: the text input, a clear button and a chevron, in one bordered box. Give it `aria-label`, or pair it with a Label through `id`.
- `ComboboxChips` — The multi-value field: chips for what is picked, then the input. Backspace in an empty input removes the last chip; Left Arrow moves onto the chips.
- `ComboboxChip` — One picked value inside ComboboxChips, with its own remove button.
- `ComboboxChipsInput` — The input inside ComboboxChips; it takes the rest of the row.
- `type ComboboxContentProps`
- `ComboboxContent` — The options panel under the field, as wide as the field; renders its own portal.
- `ComboboxList` — The scrolling list. Pass a function child to render each of `items`; it is called for the filtered ones only.
- `ComboboxItem` — One option. `value` is the item itself; a check marks the selected one(s).
- `ComboboxEmpty` — Shown in place of the list when nothing matches the typed text.
- `ComboboxGroupLabel` — Heading for a ComboboxGroup.
- `ComboboxSeparator` — Horizontal rule between groups.

---

# CommandButton

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { CommandButton, type CommandButtonProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A borderless command for toolbars and command bars: text and icon neutral
at rest; on hover a grey fill and the icon in the brand colour, as on a
Button. Put the icon before the text as a child. As a menu trigger it adds
a chevron by itself, and while the menu is open keeps a pressed fill and
the brand-coloured icon. Pass `render` to make it a link.

## Example

```tsx
<CommandButton onClick={share}><ShareIcon />Share</CommandButton>

<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<CommandButton />}><PlusIcon />New item</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="start">
    <DropdownMenuItem><MailIcon />Email message</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Parts

- `type CommandButtonProps`

# DataTable

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

Needs the optional peer `@tanstack/react-table`. It is **not** exported from the root `turkishcoffee` entry.

```tsx
import { DataTable, actionsColumn, DataTableSkeleton, dataTableFeatures, dataTableLabelsForLocale, defaultDataTableLabels, type DataTableProps, type ActionsColumnOptions, type DataTableSkeletonProps, type DataTableColumnMeta, type DataTableColumnFilter, type DataTableFilterVariant, type DataTableFilterControlProps, type DataTableFeatures, type DataTableColumn, type DataTableLabels, type DataTablePagination, type DataTableRowSelection, type DataTableColumnSelection, type DataTableQuery, type DataTableQueryChange, type DataTableServer, type DataTableSelectionOptions, type DataTableColumnSelectionOptions, type DataTableLayoutOptions, type DataTableExportRows, type DataTableExportColumns, type DataTableExportScope, type DataTableExportRequest, type DataTableExportOptions, type DataTableExportData, type DataTableHandle } from 'turkishcoffee/data-table'
```

A data grid over TanStack Table v9. Every
interaction is one boolean away — `sortable`, `resizable` (with Excel's
double-click-to-fit), `reorderable`, `hideable`, `selectable`,
`selectableColumns`, `filterable`, `exportable` — and a feature's options
and state sit in its own prop, as an object in place of `true`. Sorting,
filters and page are one value, the query: controlled (`query` +
`onQueryChange`) or left to the grid (`defaultQuery`). Client-side by
default; `server` hands the query to a backend. Import from
`turkishcoffee/data-table`. For a static table use the root `Table`
primitives instead. Selected rows are grey; `selectable={{ color: 'primary' }}`
tints them with the brand. `striped` alternates the body rows between
`--table-row-odd` and `--table-row-even`, including virtualized rows; hover
and selection override the alternating background.

Use `toolbar` for search and status filters beside the column controls. When
rows or columns are selected, an inline bar groups the selection count,
export (when enabled) and a visible clear-selection button above the grid.

Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop. Arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End and
PageUp/PageDown move the active cell; F2 (or Enter on a cell without its own
action) moves focus into the cell's controls and Escape returns to the grid.
Enter sorts a header, Alt+↓ opens its menu, Shift+Space selects a row,
Ctrl+Space a column, Ctrl+A every row. In `dir="rtl"` the arrows follow the
reading direction.

Not supported: grouped (nested) column headers, footers, cell editing, tree
rows and variable-height rows. Rows are fixed-height and single-line, and
`columns` must be leaf columns.

## Example

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumn<Payment>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  {
    accessorKey: 'amount',
    header: 'Amount',
    cell: (info) => `$${info.getValue<number>().toFixed(2)}`,
    meta: { align: 'end' },
  },
]

<DataTable aria-label="Payments" columns={columns} data={payments} sortable resizable reorderable hideable pageSize={25} />
```

## More examples

### Server data: one query, one request

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState<DataTableQuery>({
sorting: [], columnFilters: [], pagination: { pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 25 },
})
const { data, isFetching, error } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['orders', query], queryFn: () => fetchOrders(query) })

<DataTable
aria-label="Orders"
columns={columns}
data={data?.rows ?? []}
getRowId={(row) => row.id} // required with server + selectable
server={{ rowCount: data?.total ?? 0 }}
loading={isFetching}
errorMessage={error ? 'Orders could not be loaded.' : undefined}
sortable filterable selectable
// A sort on page 3 arrives here once, already on page 1.
query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery}
exportable={{
// The grid writes the file from rows the app fetches...
fetchRows: (request) => api.fetchOrdersForExport(request),
onError: () => toast.error('Export failed'),
}}
/>
```

### Restricted selection

```tsx
// Only open invoices can be selected. The backend counts them, so "every
// matching row" stays available; it checks eligibility again when it acts.
<DataTable aria-label="Invoices" columns={columns} data={page} getRowId={(row) => row.id}
server={{ rowCount }}
selectable={{ isRowSelectable: (row) => row.status === 'open', selectableRowCount: openCount, scopeKey: search }} />
```

### Custom filter control and toolbar

```tsx
const MinimumAmount = ({ value, onApply, close }: DataTableFilterControlProps) => (
<form onSubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); onApply(Number(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('min'))) }}>
<Input name="min" type="number" defaultValue={typeof value === 'number' ? value : ''} />
<Button type="submit">Apply</Button> <Button variant="ghost" onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
</form>
)
const columns: DataTableColumn<Invoice>[] = [{
accessorKey: 'amount', header: 'Amount',
filterFn: (row, id, min) => row.getValue<number>(id) >= (min as number),
meta: { align: 'end', filter: { control: MinimumAmount } },
}]

<DataTable aria-label="Invoices" columns={columns} data={invoices} filterable
toolbar={<Button size="sm" onClick={openNewInvoice}>New invoice</Button>} />
```

### Server export written by the backend

```tsx
<DataTable aria-label="Orders" columns={columns} data={page} server={{ rowCount }}
exportable={{
onServerExport: async (request, format) => download(await api.exportOrders(request, format)),
onError: () => toast.error('Export failed'),
}} />
```

### Imperative export with error handling

```tsx
const ref = useRef<DataTableHandle<Invoice>>(null)
try {
await ref.current?.export('xlsx', { rows: 'loaded' })
} catch {
// Already reported to exportable.onError; the promise rejects as well.
}
```

### Turkish locale, right-to-left, printing

```tsx
// Locale drives sorting, the "contains" filter, numeric labels and exports (default en-US).
<DataTable aria-label="Çalışanlar" locale="tr-TR" columns={columns} data={rows} />
<DataTable aria-label="الموظفون" dir="rtl" columns={columns} data={rows} />
// Every row in normal flow (no virtualization), e.g. for a print view.
<DataTable aria-label="Report" rowVirtualization={false} columns={columns} data={rows} />
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `DataTableProps`

- `columns: Array<DataTableColumn<TData>>` — TanStack Table v9 column definitions: `DataTableColumn<Row>[]`.
- `getRowId?: (row: TData, index: number) => string` — A stable id per row (e.g. `(row) => row.id`). Defaults to the row's index. Needed for selections that outlive a sort, new data or a page change.
- `sortable?: boolean` — Click a header to sort: ascending → descending → off; Shift+click adds a second sort. Numbers, dates and booleans compare by value, text in the page's language, and blanks always go last. Opt a column out with `enableSorting: false`, or give it its own `sortFn`. With `server`, the server sorts.
- `multiSort?: boolean` — Whether Shift+click adds a second sort (default `true`). `false` keeps one sort column, Shift or not — for a backend that sorts by one column, so the grid never shows a sort the server ignores.
- `resizable?: boolean` — Drag a column's right edge to resize it; double-click the edge to fit the column to its content, as in Excel. Opt out per column with `enableResizing: false`; bound it with `minSize` / `maxSize`.
- `reorderable?: boolean` — Drag a header to move its column. Keep a column in place with `meta: { reorderable: false }`.
- `hideable?: boolean` — Adds a "Columns" menu to show and hide columns. Opt a column out with `enableHiding: false`.
- `selectable?: boolean | 'hover' | DataTableSelectionOptions<TData>` — Adds a checkbox column. `true`: boxes always visible; `'hover'`: a row's box shows on hover, every box once anything is selected. The header box works in two steps: this page, then every row matching the query (on the server too); Shift+click selects a range. Options — the scope, the eligible rows, the controlled selection — in {@link DataTableSelectionOptions}.
- `striped?: boolean` — Alternate the body rows' background. Off by default.
- `selectableColumns?: boolean | DataTableColumnSelectionOptions` — Excel's column selection, from the thin strip above the headers. The first click covers this page, the second every row, the third clears; Ctrl/⌘ adds a column, Shift a range, Escape clears.
- `filterable?: boolean` — A filter per column, behind a funnel that shows on header hover: a checklist, Min and Max, a calendar or "contains", by the column's `meta.filter` or its values. Opt out per column with `enableColumnFilter: false`, or give one its own `filterFn`. With `server`, the server filters.
- `exportable?: boolean | DataTableExportOptions<TData>` — Adds the toolbar's Export menu (CSV or Excel). It writes the selected columns (else the visible ones) of the selected rows (else the rows the column selection covers, else every filtered row). With `server`, rows beyond the loaded page come from `fetchRows`, or the backend writes the file through `onServerExport` ({@link DataTableExportOptions}).
- `height?: number` — Total height in px. Setting it virtualizes the rows with react-window: only the visible ones are in the DOM. Without it, rows render in normal flow — up to 100; past that (a page size of 200 or All) the grid virtualizes on its own, at most 640px of rows tall.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Row density: `sm` 32px, `md` 44px (compact and comfortable).
- `columnVirtualization?: boolean | 'auto'` — Render only the columns in view (plus some overscan) on each row. `'auto'` (default) turns it on past 30 visible columns, where scrolling would otherwise render every cell of every row that comes into view.
- `stickyHeader?: boolean | { top: number }` — The header row sticks to the top of the page while the rows scroll by (default). `{ top }` leaves room for a fixed bar above it; `false` turns it off.
- `pageSize?: TablePageSize` — Rows per page; turns on the pagination bar. The uncontrolled query's starting size: changing it later applies the new size and returns to the first page. `'all'` is not offered with `server`. Server pages default to 25.
- `pageSizeOptions?: TablePageSize[]` — Choices in the page-size picker. Defaults to 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 and All (All left out with `server`).
- `server?: DataTableServer` — Server-side data: `data` is the current page; the backend sorts, filters and pages it from the query (`onQueryChange`). DataTable never sorts or filters a loaded page by itself.
- `layout?: DataTableLayoutOptions` — Where the column layout (widths, order, visibility) is kept: `storageKey` (this browser), or `saved` + `onChange` (a cookie, a backend), and the `defaults` it resets to. {@link DataTableLayoutOptions}
- `query?: DataTableQuery` — The controlled query. With it the app owns sorting, filters and page: the grid shows exactly this and asks for changes through `onQueryChange`. Without it the grid keeps the query, from `defaultQuery`.
- `defaultQuery?: Partial<DataTableQuery>` — The uncontrolled query's starting value, read once. Also where `ref.resetQuery()` returns.
- `onQueryChange?: (query: DataTableQuery, change: DataTableQueryChange) => void` — Every change to the query, whole: a new sort or filter also returns to the first page, in the same call. `change` says which part the user changed. On the server, fetch exactly `query` — one change, one request.
- `rowVirtualization?: boolean | 'auto'` — Render only a window of rows. false keeps all rows in normal document flow; auto uses height or the 100-row threshold.
- `autoSize?: 'initial' | 'data' | false` — Fit once (default), fit after data changes, or use explicit/default widths. User sizes always win.
- `toolbar?: React.ReactNode` — Custom content beside the built-in toolbar controls.
- `loading?: boolean` — A request is in flight: a bar runs under the header, the grid is `aria-busy`, paging pauses, and with no rows yet placeholder rows show.
- `loadingMessage?: React.ReactNode` — Initial loading content, outside the grid's data-row count.
- `errorMessage?: React.ReactNode` — Error content; takes precedence over loading and empty content.
- `'aria-label'?: string` — Accessible name of the grid. Supply this or aria-labelledby.
- `'aria-labelledby'?: string` — ID of the visible heading naming the grid.
- `'aria-describedby'?: string` — ID of instructions describing the grid.
- `dir?: 'ltr' | 'rtl'` — Explicit reading direction; defaults to ltr.
- `ref?: React.Ref<DataTableHandle<TData>>` — Imperative access: resets, paging, selected rows, export data.
- `locale?: string` — Locale for the words the grid renders, sorting, filtering, numerals and exports. Defaults to LocaleProvider's, else the page's `<html lang>`, else en-US. English and Turkish words ship complete.
- `emptyMessage?: React.ReactNode` — Shown in place of rows when `data` is empty. Defaults to "No results."
- `labels?: Partial<DataTableLabels>` — Single words to replace, over the locale's own.
- `onRowClick?: (row: TData) => void` — Makes rows clickable (and focusable, Enter activates). Clicks on buttons and links inside a row are ignored.
- `className?: string` — Applied to the outer wrapper (toolbar + grid + pagination row).

### `ActionsColumnOptions`

- `label: string` — The column's name: read by screen readers in place of a visible header, and shown in the Columns menu.
- `cell: (context: CellContext<DataTableFeatures, TData, unknown>) => ReactNode` — The row's actions, usually a DropdownMenu opened by a ghost `size="icon"` Button with an `aria-label` naming the row; `size="icon-sm"` in a `size="sm"` grid, whose 32px rows a 36px button overflows.
- `size?: number` — Width in px. Default 56: a 36px icon button with room on both sides.
- `id?: string` — Default `'actions'`.

### `DataTableSkeletonProps`

- `columns?: number | readonly string[]` — The headers to show, as the real table will (`['Name', 'Email']`), or how many columns to sketch. Default 5.
- `rows?: number` — Placeholder rows. Default 8.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Row height, as DataTable's `size`: `sm` 32px or `md` 44px (default).
- `selectable?: boolean` — A checkbox column first, as DataTable's `selectable`.
- `label?: string` — Announced to screen readers. Defaults to "Loading…" in the page's language (see LocaleProvider).

### `DataTableColumnMeta`

- `headerClassName?: string` — Header classes, merged last.
- `cellClassName?: string` — Cell classes, merged last. Rows remain fixed-height and single-line.
- `filter?: DataTableColumnFilter` — The column's header filter. Filtering, cell display and export are set apart: none reads the others.
- `align?: 'start' | 'end'` — `'end'` right-aligns the header and cells — use it for numbers.
- `label?: string` — The column's name in the Columns menu and header menu when `header` is a function.
- `reorderable?: boolean` — `false` keeps the column where it is when `reorderable` is on (an actions column).
- `exportValue?: (row: TData) => unknown` — The value written to CSV/Excel for a row, when the cell's own value is not what should be exported — e.g. `(row) => row.isActive ? 'Active' : 'Passive'` for a Badge column, or anything for a display column with no accessor. `row` is the column's row type.

### `DataTableColumnFilter`

- `options?: readonly TableColumnFilterOption[]` — The column's known values (a status, a type): the filter becomes a checklist of them. Tick the values to show; nothing ticked is no filter, and the filter value is the array of ticked values. A `count` shows beside its option; on the client, options without one are counted. On the server, `options` variant needs them: a page holds only some values.
- `control?: ComponentType<DataTableFilterControlProps>` — A filter editor of your own inside the header popover. Values need not be strings. Wins over `variant` and `options`.

### `DataTableLabels`

- `columns: string` — The column chooser button and its menu heading.
- `resetLayout: string` — Column chooser item that undoes resizing, reordering and hiding.
- `autofit: string` — Header menu item that fits the column to its content.
- `columnMenu: (column: string) => string` — Accessible name of a header's menu button.
- `resizeColumn: (column: string) => string` — Accessible name of a column's resize handle.
- `filter: (column: string) => string` — Column filter title and trigger name: "Filter Name".
- `filterContains: string` — Caption above the filter input.
- `clearFilters: string` — Toolbar button that clears every column filter, shown while one is set.
- `filterSearchOptions: string` — An options filter's search field, from six options.
- `filterNoOptions: string` — An options filter when its search matches none.
- `filterMin: string` — A number filter's lower bound.
- `filterMax: string` — A number filter's upper bound.
- `filterPickDates: string` — A date filter before a day is picked.
- `filterTrue: string` — A boolean column's checklist options, without `exportValue` to name them.
- `selectAll: string` — Accessible name of the header checkbox.
- `selectAllRows: (count: number) => string` — The step from "this page" to "everything": the header box's name once the page is selected, and the toolbar's shortcut.
- `selectColumn: (column: string) => string` — Accessible name of a column's selection strip.
- `columnScopePage: (rows: number) => string` — A column selection that covers the rows on this page.
- `columnScopeAll: (rows: number) => string` — A column selection that covers every row.
- `selectRow: string` — Accessible name of a row checkbox.
- `rowsHiddenByFilter: (count: number) => string` — Selected rows the current filters hide, shown beside the count.
- `rowsOffPage: (count: number) => string` — Server mode: selected rows not in the loaded page, shown beside the count.
- `clearSelection: string` — Label of the button clearing selected rows and columns.
- `exportError: string` — Export failure, displayed as an inline alert.
- `loading: string` — Initial loading status.
- `empty: string` — Empty grid status.
- `sortDescription: (direction: 'asc' | 'desc', priority: number) => string` — Accessible description of secondary sorting.
- `exportScope: (columns: number, rows: number, scope: DataTableExportScope) => string` — Heading of the export menu: what will be written. `scope` says which rows: `selected`, `page` (on screen), `filtered` (every row passing the filters) or `loaded`.
- `exportLoadedOnly: (columns: number, rows: number, scope: DataTableExportScope) => string` — Export menu heading when the rows live on the server but no server export is set up: only the loaded ones are written.

### `DataTableQuery`

- `pagination?: DataTablePagination` — Absent when the grid has no pages (no `pageSize`, no `server`).

### `DataTableServer`

- `rowCount: number` — Rows matching the current query on the server.

### `DataTableSelectionOptions`

- `checkboxes?: 'always' | 'hover'` — `'always'` (default): every row shows its box. `'hover'`: a row's box shows on hover, every box once anything is selected.
- `color?: 'neutral' | 'primary'` — The selected rows' background: `'neutral'` (default) grey, `'primary'` the brand's soft tint.
- `isRowSelectable?: (row: TData) => boolean` — Which rows may be selected.
- `defaultValue?: DataTableRowSelection` — The uncontrolled selection's starting value, read once.
- `scopeKey?: string` — The query's parts that live outside the grid (a search box, status tabs), as one string. Changing it clears an `allMatching` selection, as the grid's own filters do, and an export request carries it.
- `selectableRowCount?: number` — Server with `isRowSelectable`: how many rows matching the query may be selected, counted by the backend. With it the header box can select every matching row, and the backend checks eligibility when it acts on the selection. Without it the selection stays explicit ids of loaded rows.

### `DataTableLayoutOptions`

- `defaults?: Partial<DataTableLayout>` — The layout the grid starts from and resets to.
- `onChange?: (layout: DataTableLayout | null) => void` — Called after an edit is complete (a resize at pointer release, not every pixel), and with `null` after a reset.
- `saved: Partial<DataTableLayout> | null` — A layout the app saved from `onChange`; `null`: nothing saved yet. Malformed fields and unknown columns are ignored.

### `DataTableExportRequest`

- `columns: string[]` — Column ids, in display order.
- `sorting: SortingState` — The order to write the rows in.
- `rows.type: 'ids'` — Exactly these rows, whatever the current filters: rows picked one by one, perhaps on other pages or searches.
- `rows.type: 'matching'` — Every row matching the query, except `excludedIds`.
- `rows.scopeKey?: string` — The selection's `scopeKey`: the app's filters outside the grid.

### `DataTableExportOptions`

- `onError?: (error: unknown, format: TableExportFormat) => void` — Toolbar and `ref.export` failures, the app's own included. `ref.export` also rejects.
- `fetchRows: (request: DataTableExportRequest) => Promise<TData[]>` — Server mode: the rows `request` describes, in the order to write them.
- `onServerExport: (request: DataTableExportRequest, format: TableExportFormat) => void | Promise<void>` — Server mode: have the backend write `request` as `format`, and download it.

### `DataTableExportData`

- `columns: Array<TableExportColumn<TData>>` — They read any row of `TData`, including rows fetched for `request`.
- `rows: TData[]` — The covered rows DataTable holds, in display order.
- `scope: DataTableExportScope` — Which rows are covered, e.g. to say "3 selected rows" before writing.
- `request: DataTableExportRequest | null` — Set when some covered rows are only on the server (server mode). Null when the grid holds them all.

### `DataTableHandle`

- `fitColumns: (columnIds?: string[]) => void` — Fit rendered content and a sample of up to 50 loaded values. Omit ids to fit visible columns.
- `resetQuery: () => void` — Back to `defaultQuery`: one change, reported once.
- `resetLayout: () => void` — Column visibility, order and sizing back to `layout.defaults`, and the stored copy removed.
- `getSelectedRows: () => TData[]` — The selected rows DataTable holds (under `allMatching`: the loaded matching rows not excluded).
- `export: (format: TableExportFormat, options?: { rows?: DataTableExportRows; columns?: DataTableExportColumns }) => Promise<void>` — Exports as the toolbar's menu does. Rows beyond the loaded data go to `exportable.fetchRows` or `onServerExport`; without either the promise rejects unless `rows` is `'page'` or `'loaded'`. Failures also reach `exportable.onError`.

## Parts

- `type DataTableProps` — Public grid props. Server selection requires a stable row identity.
- `type ActionsColumnOptions`
- `actionsColumn` — The column for a row's actions. It has a fixed width, a centred cell and a header only screen readers read. It cannot be sorted, filtered, resized, hidden, moved or exported. Put it last.

  ```tsx
  const columns: DataTableColumn<Person>[] = [
    { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
    actionsColumn<Person>({
      label: 'Actions',
      cell: ({ row }) => (
        <DropdownMenu>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={`Actions for ${row.original.name}`} />}>
            <EllipsisIcon />
          </DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent align="end">…</DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      ),
    }),
  ]
  ```

- `type DataTableSkeletonProps`
- `DataTableSkeleton` — A DataTable on its way: the bordered frame, the header, and rows of Skeleton bars at DataTable's own row height, so nothing jumps when the real table arrives. Use it where the table can't render yet, such as a Suspense fallback around a server fetch. DataTable draws the same rows itself while it loads with no rows. The bars share Skeleton's glint, so the table loads as one surface.

  ```tsx
  <Suspense fallback={<DataTableSkeleton columns={['Name', 'Email', 'Status']} selectable />}>
    <Employees />
  </Suspense>
  ```

- `type DataTableColumnMeta` — What DataTable reads from a column's `meta`. All optional. `TData` is the row type.
- `type DataTableColumnFilter` — A column's filter. Its kind comes from `variant`; unset, from the column's values — a convenience, held once seen: a column of Dates gets a calendar, of numbers Min and Max, of booleans a checklist, anything else "contains". An empty page or a page of blanks never changes it. Set `variant` whenever the values may not say it: dates kept as strings, a column of a few repeated values (`options`), or server data.
- `type DataTableFilterVariant` — A column filter's kind, and the value it puts in `columnFilters`: - `text` — the text the cell contains (`string`); - `options` — the values ticked (`Array<string | number | boolean>`); - `number` — `{ min?: number; max?: number }`, both inclusive; - `date` — `{ from?: Date; to?: Date }`, local days, both inclusive.
- `type DataTableFilterControlProps` — Props for a custom column filter. onApply commits and closes; close cancels.
- `dataTableFeatures` — The TanStack Table v9 feature set DataTable runs with: sorting, filtering, row selection, client pagination, column sizing/resizing, ordering and visibility. Every feature is registered; the DataTable props decide which ones the user can reach. `@tanstack/react-table` is an OPTIONAL peer, so this lives behind its own entry point (`turkishcoffee/data-table`) and never loads for projects that only import the root barrel.
- `type DataTableFeatures`
- `type DataTableColumn` — Column definitions for DataTable — carries the feature set for you. This is TanStack Table v9: type columns as `DataTableColumn<Row>[]`, not v8's `ColumnDef<Row>` or `createColumnHelper`. Per-column switches are TanStack's own: `enableSorting`, `enableResizing`, `enableHiding`, `enableColumnFilter`, `size`, `minSize`, `maxSize`, `sortFn`, `filterFn`; plus `meta` ({@link DataTableColumnMeta}).
- `type DataTableLabels` — Every word DataTable renders itself, in the language of its `locale` (else LocaleProvider's, else `<html lang>`). Override single words through the `labels` prop. The pagination words are TablePagination's, which DataTable renders.
- `dataTableLabelsForLocale` — Every DataTable word in `locale`'s language, numbers in its numerals: the same locale as the grid's sorting, filtering and exports. English and Turkish ship complete; other languages get English.
- `defaultDataTableLabels` — The English labels.
- `type DataTablePagination` — Which page is on screen. `pageIndex` is 0-based; `'all'` puts every row on one page.
- `type DataTableRowSelection` — Which rows are selected. Plain data: store it, or send it to a backend as is. - `ids`: these rows, on any page — picked one by one, or a whole page (the header box's first click adds the page's ids). - `allMatching`: every row matching the query — loaded or not, on the server too — except `excludedIds`. The header box's second click.
- `type DataTableColumnSelection` — Which columns are selected, and over which rows: the page on screen, or every matching row.
- `type DataTableQuery` — What the rows on screen answer to: their order, their filters and their page. One value, so a change that touches two of them — a new sort also returns to the first page — is one change, reported once. On the server it is what the backend is asked for.
- `type DataTableQueryChange` — Which part of the query a change started from. A sort or filter change also returns to the first page; `reset` is `ref.resetQuery()`.
- `type DataTableServer` — Server-side data: `data` is the current page, and sorting, filtering and paging happen on the server, through `onQueryChange`. DataTable never sorts or filters a loaded page on its own, and never reads totals, filter options or selection counts off the one page it holds.
- `type DataTableSelectionOptions` — Row selection: `selectable={true}`, `'hover'`, or these options. Every option is optional; `value` + `onChange` control the selection, or leave it to the grid from `defaultValue`. What survives what, with `scope: 'crossPage'` (default): - rows picked one by one (`ids`) survive paging, sorting, filtering and new searches. Picked rows a filter hides stay selected, and an export of the selection still writes them. - every matching row (`allMatching`) describes one result: it clears when the filters or `scopeKey` change, and survives paging and sorting. With `scope: 'page'`, changing the page, the sorting or the filters clears the selection, and the header box selects the page only.
- `type DataTableColumnSelectionOptions` — Column selection: `selectableColumns={true}`, or these options to control or start it.
- `type DataTableLayoutOptions` — Where the column layout (widths, order, visibility) is kept — one of two ways, never both: - `storageKey`: in this browser's `localStorage`, by the grid; - `saved` + `onChange`: by the app, in a cookie or a backend. Read on the server, the page renders in the saved layout from the first byte. Precedence: the saved layout > `defaults` > the column definitions. A saved layout is fitted to the current columns: columns removed since it was saved are dropped, new ones take their place from the definitions, and a column whose `id` changed counts as new. "Reset layout" returns to `defaults` (else the definitions), clears the stored copy and reports `null`.
- `type DataTableExportRows` — The rows an export covers. `auto`: selected rows, else the column selection's rows, else every filtered row.
- `type DataTableExportColumns` — The columns an export covers. `auto`: the selected columns, else the visible ones.
- `type DataTableExportScope` — Which rows an export covers once `auto` is resolved: the selected rows, the rows on screen, every row passing the filters (`allMatching` included), or all of `data`.
- `type DataTableExportRequest` — Server mode: the rows an export covers that the loaded page doesn't hold, described for the backend.
- `type DataTableExportOptions` — The Export menu (`exportable={true}` or these options). Rows the grid holds it writes itself. In server mode rows beyond the loaded page are the app's to provide, one of two ways: - `fetchRows`: the app fetches them; the grid writes the file; - `onServerExport`: the backend writes the file; the app downloads it. With neither, the menu writes the loaded rows and says so.
- `type DataTableExportData` — Export-ready data: hand `columns` and `rows` to `exportTable`, or `request` to your backend.
- `type DataTableHandle` — Imperative access: `<DataTable ref={ref} />`. A controlled value changes through its `onChange` / `onQueryChange`.

---

# DatePicker

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { DatePicker, DateRangePicker, type DatePickerProps, type DateRangePickerProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Controlled single-date picker. Works as a `FormControl` child.

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `ResponsivePickerProps`

- `title: string` — Accessible name for the drawer; the popover is labelled by its trigger.

### `DatePickerProps`

- `formatStr?: string` — date-fns format string for the trigger label.
- `locale?: Locale` — A date-fns locale (e.g. `tr` from `react-day-picker/locale`) for the label and the calendar. Defaults to LocaleProvider's language, else `<html lang>`.

## Parts

- `type DatePickerProps`
- `type DateRangePickerProps`
- `DateRangePicker` — Controlled date-range picker. Stays open until both ends are picked.
