# Dialog

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogClose, DialogPortal, DialogOverlay, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogFooter, DialogTitle, DialogDescription } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Modal for a focused task (a form, details): centered on `sm` screens and up,
a Base UI bottom drawer below. Every part reads the mode from here, so the same
markup works in both. Closes on outside click and Escape (and a swipe down on
mobile). For confirming a destructive action use AlertDialog; for a panel
sliding from an edge use Sheet. DialogTitle is required for accessibility.

## Example

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Edit profile</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Edit profile</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Changes are saved when you click Save.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    …
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `showCloseButton?: boolean` — Render the × button in the top-right corner (desktop only). Defaults to true.

## Parts

- `DialogTrigger` — Opens the Dialog. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button the trigger.
- `DialogClose` — Closes the Dialog. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button close it.
- `DialogPortal` — Portal used by DialogContent. Rarely needed directly.
- `DialogOverlay` — Backdrop behind the Dialog. Already rendered by DialogContent.
- `DialogContent` — The dialog panel. Renders its own portal, overlay and a close (×) button (a bottom drawer without the × on mobile); pass `showCloseButton={false}` to drop the ×. Widen with `className="sm:max-w-2xl"`.
- `DialogHeader` — Stacks DialogTitle and DialogDescription.
- `DialogFooter` — Action row; stacks on mobile, right-aligns from `sm`.
- `DialogTitle` — Required: names the dialog for screen readers.
- `DialogDescription` — Muted text under DialogTitle.

---

# Drawer

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Drawer, DrawerTrigger, DrawerClose, DrawerPortal, DrawerOverlay, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerFooter, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Bottom sheet built on Base UI's Drawer: slides up from the bottom edge and
closes on a swipe down, outside tap or Escape. Dialog already becomes one on
mobile, so reach for Drawer directly only when you want a drawer on every
screen size. DrawerTitle is required for accessibility.

## Example

```tsx
<Drawer>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button />}>Filters</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Narrow the list.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    …
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

## Parts

- `DrawerTrigger` — Opens the Drawer. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button the trigger.
- `DrawerClose` — Closes the Drawer. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button close it.
- `DrawerPortal` — Portal used by DrawerContent. Rarely needed directly.
- `DrawerOverlay` — Backdrop behind the Drawer; fades with the swipe. Already rendered by DrawerContent.
- `DrawerContent` — Bottom sheet with a drag handle. Base UI drives the enter, exit and swipe motion.
- `DrawerHeader` — Stacks DrawerTitle and DrawerDescription.
- `DrawerFooter` — Action row pinned to the bottom of the Drawer.
- `DrawerTitle` — Required: names the drawer for screen readers.
- `DrawerDescription` — Muted text under DrawerTitle.

---

# DropdownMenu

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuSubContent, type DropdownMenuContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Menu of actions opened from a trigger. Built on Base UI's Menu. For choosing a
form value use Select.

## Example

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Options</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
    <DropdownMenuLabel>Project</DropdownMenuLabel>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={rename}>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem tone="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `tone?: 'neutral' | 'danger'` — `danger` colours the item for dangerous actions like Delete.

## Parts

- `DropdownMenuTrigger` — Opens the menu. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button the trigger.
- `DropdownMenuGroup` — Groups related items.
- `DropdownMenuSub` — Wraps a DropdownMenuSubTrigger and DropdownMenuSubContent for a nested menu.
- `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` — Holds DropdownMenuRadioItems; controlled with `value` + `onValueChange`.
- `type DropdownMenuContentProps`
- `DropdownMenuContent` — The menu panel; renders its own portal. Pass `anchor` (an element or ref) to position it against something other than the trigger.
- `DropdownMenuItem` — One action. Run it with `onClick`; the menu closes afterwards. `tone="danger"` colours it for dangerous actions.
- `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` — A toggleable item; controlled with `checked` + `onCheckedChange`.
- `DropdownMenuRadioItem` — One option inside a DropdownMenuRadioGroup.
- `DropdownMenuLabel` — Non-interactive heading inside the menu. A plain element, so it works anywhere in the menu, inside a DropdownMenuGroup or not.
- `DropdownMenuSeparator` — Horizontal rule between groups of items.
- `DropdownMenuShortcut` — Right-aligned keyboard hint inside an item, e.g. `⌘K`. Display only.
- `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` — Item that opens a nested DropdownMenuSubContent.
- `DropdownMenuSubContent` — The nested menu panel; opens beside its DropdownMenuSubTrigger.

---

# EmptyState

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { EmptyState, type EmptyStateProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Placeholder for a list or page that has no content yet: icon, title,
description and a call to action.

## Example

```tsx
<EmptyState
  icon={<InboxIcon />}
  title="No invoices yet"
  description="Invoices you create will show up here."
  action={<Button>New invoice</Button>}
/>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Pass any icon element — the package pins no icon library.
- `title: React.ReactNode` — Required: one short line saying what is missing.
- `description?: React.ReactNode` — Muted text under the title: why it is empty or what to do next.
- `action?: React.ReactNode` — Buttons or links rendered under the description.

## Parts

- `type EmptyStateProps`

# FileUpload

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { fileUploadLabelsForLocale, defaultFileUploadLabels, formatFileSize, FileUpload, FileUploadDropzone, FileUploadTrigger, FileUploadList, FileUploadItem, type FileRejectionReason, type FileRejection, type FileUploadLabels, type FileUploadProps, type FileUploadDropzoneProps, type FileUploadItemProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Picks files by drag-and-drop, click or keyboard and checks them against
`accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`. It holds no list and uploads nothing:
`onFilesAdded` hands over the accepted `File`s, the app keeps them in state
(with any upload progress) and renders them as FileUploadItems.
Rejections go to `onFilesRejected` and are announced to screen readers.

## Example

```tsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([])

<FileUpload accept=".pdf,image/*" maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024} maxFiles={5} fileCount={files.length}
  onFilesAdded={(added) => setFiles((current) => [...current, ...added])}
  onFilesRejected={(rejections) => toast.error(`${rejections.length} files were not added`)}>
  <FileUploadDropzone description="PDF or image, up to 10 MB" />
  <FileUploadList>
    {files.map((file) => (
      <FileUploadItem key={file.name} file={file}
        onRemove={() => setFiles((current) => current.filter((f) => f !== file))} />
    ))}
  </FileUploadList>
</FileUpload>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `FileUploadLabels`

- `title: string` — The drop zone's main line.
- `dropping: string` — The drop zone's main line while files are dragged over it.
- `added: (count: number) => string` — Announced after files are added.
- `rejected: (rejection: FileRejection) => string` — Announced (and passed nowhere else) for each rejected file.

### `FileUploadProps`

- `accept?: string` — File types to take, as in `<input accept>`: extensions, MIME types or `image/*`.
- `multiple?: boolean` — Take several files at once. Defaults to true.
- `maxSize?: number` — Largest file in bytes.
- `maxFiles?: number` — Most files to take, counting `fileCount` already held.
- `fileCount?: number` — How many files the app already holds, so `maxFiles` counts them.
- `onFilesAdded: (files: File[]) => void` — The files that passed `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`.
- `onFilesRejected?: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void` — The files that did not, with the reason.
- `name?: string` — `name` for the hidden input, to submit files with a plain form.

### `FileUploadDropzoneProps`

- `title?: React.ReactNode` — Replaces the main line ("Drag files here or click to browse").
- `description?: React.ReactNode` — What is accepted, e.g. "PDF or image, up to 10 MB".
- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Replaces the cloud icon.

### `FileUploadItemProps`

- `file: File | { name: string; size: number }` — The file, or just its name and size for files already on the server.
- `progress?: number` — 0–100 while uploading; leave out when there is no upload or it is done.
- `error?: React.ReactNode` — Shown in place of the size, in the danger colour, when the upload failed.
- `onRemove?: () => void` — Adds a remove button.
- `removeLabel?: string` — Accessible name of the remove button. Defaults to "Remove" followed by the file name.
- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Replaces the file icon, e.g. with an image preview.
- `actions?: React.ReactNode` — Extra controls before the remove button, e.g. a retry or download button.

## Parts

- `type FileRejectionReason` — Why a file was turned away.
- `type FileRejection`
- `type FileUploadLabels`
- `fileUploadLabelsForLocale` — The labels in `locale`'s language.
- `defaultFileUploadLabels` — The English labels.
- `formatFileSize` — "412 KB", "1.2 MB": a file size in the units people read.
- `type FileUploadProps`
- `type FileUploadDropzoneProps`
- `FileUploadDropzone` — The drop area. Click it, or focus it and press Enter or Space, to browse; drag files onto it to add them. Pass children to replace its content.
- `FileUploadTrigger` — Opens the file picker from your own control, e.g. a Button in a toolbar. Pass `render` to use another element.

  ```tsx
  <FileUploadTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}><UploadIcon />Upload</FileUploadTrigger>
  ```

- `FileUploadList` — The list of files under the drop zone.
- `type FileUploadItemProps`
- `FileUploadItem` — One file: icon, name, size or error, an optional progress bar and a remove button.

---

# Form

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

Needs the optional peer `react-hook-form`. It is **not** exported from the root `turkishcoffee` entry.

```tsx
import { Form, FormField, useFormField, FormItem, FormLabel, FormControl, FormDescription, FormMessage, FormErrorSummary, FormTabs, FormTabsList, FormTabsTrigger, FormTabsContent, FormTabsActions, FormTabsNext, FormTabsPrevious, useFormTabs, type FormStepState, type FormTabsLabels } from 'turkishcoffee/form'
```

react-hook-form's FormProvider. Imported from `turkishcoffee/form`, not the
root: `react-hook-form` is an OPTIONAL peer, so this lives behind its own entry
point and never loads for projects that only import the root barrel.

## Example

```tsx
const form = useForm<Values>({ defaultValues: { email: '' } })

<Form {...form}>
  <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)} className="flex flex-col gap-4">
    <FormField
      control={form.control}
      name="email"
      rules={{ required: 'Email is required' }}
      render={({ field }) => (
        <FormItem>
          <FormLabel>Email</FormLabel>
          <FormControl><Input type="email" {...field} /></FormControl>
          <FormDescription>We never share it.</FormDescription>
          <FormMessage />
        </FormItem>
      )}
    />
    <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
  </form>
</Form>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `FormErrorSummary`

- `title?: (count: number) => React.ReactNode` — The heading, from the number of errors.

### `FormTabsContextValue`

- `reached: number` — Visitation history, independent of validation/completion.

### `FormTabs`

- `linear?: boolean` — A stepper: only move forwards once the steps before the target validate.

## Parts

- `FormField` — Connects one field to the form: a react-hook-form Controller plus the context the Form* parts read.
- `useFormField` — Ids and error state for the current field. Must be called inside FormField and FormItem.
- `FormItem` — Wraps one field's label, control, description and message; generates their shared id.
- `FormLabel` — Label wired to the field's control; turns red on error. Pass `info` to put an InfoLabel's info button beside it.
- `FormControl` — Wraps your input and wires up id + aria-describedby + aria-invalid. Use with any control that forwards props: <FormControl><Input /></FormControl>
- `FormDescription` — Helper text under the control.
- `FormMessage` — Renders the field's validation error, or `children` when there is none.
- `FormErrorSummary` — A danger Alert that lists every validation error after a failed submit, each a link that focuses its field — opening the FormTabs tab it sits in first. Hidden until the first submit and once every error is fixed. Put it above the fields (or the tabs), where it is seen first; worth it on long or tabbed forms, noise on a short one. Errors set on `root` are listed as text.

  ```tsx
  <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
    <FormErrorSummary />
    <FormTabs>…</FormTabs>
  </form>
  ```

- `type FormStepState` — Where a step stands in a linear form.
- `type FormTabsLabels` — Localizable navigation and status text. Button children override their label.
- `FormTabs` — Splits one react-hook-form form across tabs or steps without losing input. Every step stays mounted while hidden, so values survive switching. Each FormField inside a FormTabsContent belongs to that step: a tab with errors shows an error icon and their count, and a failed submit jumps to the first such tab and focuses the field. Add FormErrorSummary to list every error with a link that opens its tab. With `linear` it is a stepper: FormTabsList draws numbered steps instead of tabs, a step can only be left forwards once its fields (and every earlier step's) validate, validated steps show a check, and errors remain visible on every step. Editing a field clears completion for its step and subsequent steps. Navigation is locked during async validation. Use labels to translate all navigation/status text, and FormTabsActions to align Back and Next/Save. Steps are ordered as they mount. Must be inside `<Form>` and `<form>`. An unknown/removed selection falls back to the first mounted step. Controlled consumers must apply onValueChange before error focus is moved.

  ```tsx
  <Form {...form}>
    <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
      <FormTabs defaultValue="employee" linear>
        <FormTabsList>
          <FormTabsTrigger value="employee">Employee</FormTabsTrigger>
          <FormTabsTrigger value="personnel">Personnel file</FormTabsTrigger>
        </FormTabsList>
        <FormTabsContent value="employee">…FormFields…</FormTabsContent>
        <FormTabsContent value="personnel">…FormFields…</FormTabsContent>
        <FormTabsActions>
          <FormTabsPrevious />
          <FormTabsNext />
        </FormTabsActions>
      </FormTabs>
      <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
    </form>
  </Form>
  ```

- `FormTabsList` — The row of tabs, or with `linear` the row of steps. Use it in place of TabsList inside FormTabs so a stepper gets its own layout.
- `FormTabsTrigger` — A section tab or numbered step. Errors stay visible on the current step. Completed steps have passed validation; editing a field clears completion for that step and every later one. Arrow keys move focus; Enter/Space selects.
- `FormTabsContent` — One step's panel. Stays mounted while hidden, so its fields keep their values.
- `FormTabsActions` — Optional action row with a hairline divider. Previous sits left; remaining actions sit right. Supply the submit button yourself; no saving is performed.

  ```tsx
  <FormTabsActions>
    <FormTabsPrevious />
    <FormTabsNext />
    {isLast && <Button type="submit">Save</Button>}
  </FormTabsActions>
  ```

- `FormTabsNext` — Goes forwards, validating in linear mode. Busy navigation cannot be overridden by disabled={false}.
- `FormTabsPrevious` — Goes backwards without validation. Renders nothing on the first step.
- `useFormTabs` — The current step and navigation, for custom controls (e.g. show the submit button only when `isLast`). isNavigating locks custom controls during validation. getStepState reports current/invalid/complete/upcoming; use hasError separately for the active step. goTo returns false for unknown targets or cancelled/blocked navigation. Must be called inside FormTabs.

---

# HoverCard

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardTrigger, HoverCardContent, type HoverCardContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Rich preview shown when a pointer hovers a link (e.g. a user profile).
Built on Base UI's PreviewCard. Not reachable on touch devices — never put
essential content or actions in it. For a short text hint use Tooltip; for
click-to-open content use Popover.

## Example

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger href="/u/ada">@ada</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent>…</HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## Parts

- `HoverCardTrigger` — The link that opens the HoverCard on hover; renders an `<a>`, so give it `href`. Pass `render={<Link />}` for your router's link. `delay` and `closeDelay` (ms) live here.
- `type HoverCardContentProps`
- `HoverCardContent` — The card panel; renders its own portal.

---

# InfoLabel

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { InfoLabel, type InfoLabelProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A Label with an info button beside it that opens a short explanation. The
explanation opens on click, tap and Enter, so unlike a Tooltip it reaches
touch and keyboard users and may hold a link. While it is open the button's
icon fills in primary.
Every prop except `info` and `infoLabel` goes to the Label. Inside a
`turkishcoffee/form` field pass `info` to FormLabel instead.

## Example

```tsx
<InfoLabel htmlFor="iban" info="Salaries are paid into this account.">IBAN</InfoLabel>
<Input id="iban" />
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `info: React.ReactNode` — The explanation behind the info button: what the field is for, its format, where the value goes.
- `infoLabel?: string` — The info button's accessible name; screen readers read it before the label text.

## Parts

- `type InfoLabelProps`

# Input

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Input, type InputProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Single-line text field; a styled `<input>` that forwards every prop.
Server-renderable; handlers like onChange come from your own client component.
For an icon, prefix or inline button inside the field use InputGroup.

## Example

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
```

## Parts

- `type InputProps`

# InputGroup

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { InputGroup, inputGroupAddonVariants, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput, InputGroupTextarea, InputGroupButton, type InputGroupAddonProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A field that combines a control with icons, text or buttons. The group owns
the border and the focus ring; the control inside is stripped of both. That way
an icon, a prefix and a button read as one field instead of a row of separately
outlined boxes. Use InputGroupInput / InputGroupTextarea inside, not Input.

## Example

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon><SearchIcon /></InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Search…" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="end">
    <InputGroupButton>Go</InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

## Variants

| Prop | Options | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `align` | `start` · `end` | `start` |

## Parts

- `inputGroupAddonVariants` — InputGroupAddon classes as a function.
- `type InputGroupAddonProps`
- `InputGroupAddon` — Icon, text or button beside the control. `align`: `start` (default) | `end`.
- `InputGroupInput` — The `<input>` inside an InputGroup (unbordered).
- `InputGroupTextarea` — The `<textarea>` inside an InputGroup (unbordered).
- `InputGroupButton` — A Button sized for the inside of an InputGroup: defaults to `variant="ghost"` and `size="sm"`, without a shadow, so it sits inside the field rather than next to it.

# Label

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Label, type LabelProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Accessible label for a form control; link it with `htmlFor`. Inside a
`turkishcoffee/form` field use FormLabel instead, which wires `htmlFor` for you.
A native `<label>`, so it is server-renderable.

## Parts

- `type LabelProps`

# LocaleProvider

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { LocaleProvider, useLocale, LocaleText, type LocaleProviderProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

The language and locale of every component below it: the words they render
themselves (labels, screen-reader names, placeholders), and the formatting,
sorting and dates that follow the locale. English and Turkish ship complete;
any other locale gets English words with its own formatting.

Without a provider, components follow the page's `<html lang>` once they
mount. On a server-rendered page that is one render in English first: put
the provider at the root, with the same locale as `<html lang>`, to render
in the right language from the first byte.

A component's own `locale` or `labels` prop still wins over the provider.

## Example

```tsx
<html lang="tr">
  <body>
    <LocaleProvider locale="tr-TR">{children}</LocaleProvider>
  </body>
</html>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `locale: string` — A BCP 47 locale, e.g. `tr-TR`. Usually the page's own `<html lang>`.

## Parts

- `type LocaleProviderProps`
- `useLocale` — The locale to render in: `locale` when the component was given one, else the nearest LocaleProvider's, else the page's `<html lang>` (after hydration, so server and client agree on the first render), else `en-US`.
- `LocaleText` — A phrase in the current language. Lets a server component render a translated word without turning client: it passes the plain `Message` and only this leaf reads the locale.

---

# NativeSelect

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { NativeSelect, type NativeSelectProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

The platform <select>, styled to match Input. Unlike the Base UI Select
it needs no client boundary and keeps the OS picker on mobile — prefer it
inside long forms and inside server components. `size`: `sm` | `md` (default).
`className` goes on the wrapper div (use it for width); other props reach the `<select>`.

## Example

```tsx
<NativeSelect name="country" defaultValue="tr">
  <option value="tr">Türkiye</option>
  <option value="de">Germany</option>
</NativeSelect>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Height: `sm` (32px) or `md` (36px, default). Replaces the HTML `size` attribute.

## Parts

- `type NativeSelectProps`

---

# Pagination

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationPrevious, PaginationNext, PaginationEllipsis, type PaginationLinkProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Page navigation built from plain anchors, so it works with any router:
pass `href` to each link. Server-renderable.

## Example

```tsx
<Pagination>
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" /></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="?page=1">1</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>2</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationEllipsis /></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationNext href="?page=3" /></PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `isActive?: boolean` — Marks the current page: outline style and `aria-current="page"`.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'icon'` — A Button size; defaults to `icon` (square).

## Parts

- `PaginationContent` — The `<ul>` holding PaginationItems.
- `PaginationItem` — One `<li>` slot; wraps a link, Previous/Next or an ellipsis.
- `type PaginationLinkProps`
- `PaginationLink` — A page number link. `isActive` marks the current page (outline style + aria-current). `size` follows Button sizes and defaults to `icon`.
- `PaginationPrevious` — Link to the previous page; below `sm` its label is read but not shown.
- `PaginationNext` — Link to the next page; below `sm` its label is read but not shown.
- `PaginationEllipsis` — Stands in for skipped page numbers.

---

# PasswordInput

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { PasswordInput, type PasswordInputProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A password field with a button that shows what was typed. The button is a
toggle (`aria-pressed`) with one name, so a screen reader hears "Show
password, pressed" rather than a label that flips under the cursor. Every
other prop goes to the `<input>`, so it works as a `FormControl` child and
with `autoComplete="current-password"` / `"new-password"`.

## Example

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="password">Password</Label>
<PasswordInput id="password" name="password" autoComplete="current-password" required />
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `showLabel?: string` — The reveal button's name. Defaults to "Show password" in the page's language (see LocaleProvider).
- `groupClassName?: string` — Classes on the bordered field around the input. `className` styles the input.

## Parts

- `type PasswordInputProps`

# Popover

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, type PopoverContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Floating panel opened by clicking a trigger; for small forms, pickers and
extra details. Non-modal. For a hover hint use Tooltip; for a list of actions
use DropdownMenu.

## Example

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Filters</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent align="start">…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Parts

- `type PopoverContentProps`
- `PopoverContent` — The panel; renders its own portal. `w-72` by default. Pass `anchor` (an element or ref) to position it against something other than the trigger.

# RadioGroup

# SearchField

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { SearchField, type SearchFieldProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A reusable search field with a label, debounce, clear button and loading
indicator. Enter bypasses the debounce. External value changes (e.g. browser
back) replace the draft; acknowledgements of submitted searches preserve
newer typing. Routing and fetching belong to the consuming application.
Renders a search form: place it outside other forms. In a toolbar, pass
`hideLabel` and match the height of the controls beside it: `size="sm"`
among 32px CommandButtons, the default `md` in DataTable's toolbar, whose
Columns and Export buttons are 36px.

## Example

```tsx
<SearchField value={search} onSearch={setSearch} placeholder="Name, email…" />

<SearchField value={search} onSearch={setSearch} hideLabel size="sm" label="Search people" />
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `value: string` — Applied search value, e.g. from a URL. Draft text stays local until submitted.
- `onSearch: (value: string) => void` — Receives trimmed text after a pause, or immediately on Enter and clear.
- `debounceMs?: number` — Typing pause in milliseconds. Defaults to 300; 0 searches immediately.
- `loading?: boolean` — Shows a spinner while results are loading; typing remains available.
- `label?: React.ReactNode` — Input label. Defaults to "Search" in the page's language (see LocaleProvider).
- `hideLabel?: boolean` — Keeps the label for screen readers but hides it, for toolbars and top bars where the search icon and placeholder already say what the field is.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Height, to match the controls beside it: `sm` (32px) among CommandButtons and other 32px controls, `md` (36px, default) beside Buttons, as in DataTable's toolbar.
- `clearLabel?: string` — Clear button text. Defaults to "Clear" in the page's language.
- `loadingLabel?: string` — Accessible spinner label. Defaults to "Searching" in the page's language.
- `className?: string` — Classes on the search form; defaults to w-72.

## Parts

- `type SearchFieldProps`

---

# SegmentedControl

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem, SegmentedControlCount, type SegmentedControlProps, type SegmentedControlItemProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A row of mutually exclusive options that change what the page shows, such as
a list's status filter: All · Active · Inactive. One segment is always
pressed. Name the group with `aria-label`. Each segment is a toggle button
(`aria-pressed`), and the arrow keys move between them. Put a count in a
segment with SegmentedControlCount.

Use Tabs for separate views with their own panels, and RadioGroup for a
choice submitted with a form.

## Example

```tsx
<SegmentedControl aria-label="Status" value={status} onValueChange={setStatus}>
  <SegmentedControlItem value="all">All</SegmentedControlItem>
  <SegmentedControlItem value="active">
    Active <SegmentedControlCount>128</SegmentedControlCount>
  </SegmentedControlItem>
  <SegmentedControlItem value="inactive">
    Inactive <SegmentedControlCount>7</SegmentedControlCount>
  </SegmentedControlItem>
</SegmentedControl>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `SegmentedControlProps`

- `value?: Value` — The pressed segment, controlled. Pair it with `onValueChange`.
- `defaultValue?: Value` — The segment pressed at first, uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value, eventDetails: ToggleGroup.ChangeEventDetails) => void` — Called with the segment just pressed. Pressing the pressed one again changes nothing: one segment always stays pressed.

### `SegmentedControlItemProps`

- `value: Value` — Identifies the segment in the group's `value`.

## Parts

- `type SegmentedControlProps`
- `type SegmentedControlItemProps`
- `SegmentedControlItem` — One segment. Pressed, it takes the page's background and a `--field` edge, at least 3:1 against the track.
- `SegmentedControlCount` — A count beside a segment's label, in tabular figures so the segment keeps its width as the number changes.

---

# Select

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Select, SelectGroup, SelectValue, SelectTrigger, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator, type SelectContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Custom-styled dropdown for picking one value. Controlled with `value` +
`onValueChange(value, eventDetails)`. Pass `items` (a `{ value: label }` map or
`{ value, label }[]`) so SelectValue shows the chosen item's label; without it
SelectValue shows the raw value. Needs a client boundary; inside server
components or long mobile forms prefer NativeSelect.

## Example

```tsx
const plans = { free: 'Free', pro: 'Pro' }

<Select items={plans} value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <SelectTrigger className="w-48">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a plan" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="free">Free</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="pro">Pro</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Height: `sm` (32px) or `md` (36px, default) — matches Button, Input and NativeSelect.

## Parts

- `SelectGroup` — Groups SelectItems under a SelectLabel.
- `SelectValue` — Shows the selected item's label inside SelectTrigger (needs `items` on Select), or `placeholder`.
- `SelectTrigger` — The button that opens the Select. `size`: `sm` | `md` (default). Sized to its content (`w-fit`); pass `className="w-full"` to fill the row.
- `type SelectContentProps`
- `SelectContent` — The options panel; renders its own portal and scroll arrows. Opens below the trigger like a dropdown; pass `alignItemWithTrigger` for the macOS-style menu that overlaps the trigger with the selected item.
- `SelectItem` — One option. `value` may be any value, not only a string.
- `SelectLabel` — Heading for a SelectGroup.
- `SelectSeparator` — Horizontal rule between groups.

---

# Separator

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Separator, type SeparatorProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Thin horizontal or vertical (`orientation="vertical"`) rule.
Server-renderable: a plain element, no primitive needed. Decorative by
default; pass `decorative={false}` when it carries meaning.

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `decorative?: boolean` — Purely visual (the default), so screen readers skip it. Pass `false` when it carries meaning.

## Parts

- `type SeparatorProps`

# Sheet

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Sheet, SheetTrigger, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetFooter, SheetTitle, SheetDescription, type SheetContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Modal panel that slides in from an edge — navigation drawers, filters,
detail views. For a centered modal use Dialog. SheetTitle is required for
accessibility.

## Example

```tsx
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Filters</SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="left">
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle>
      <SheetDescription>Narrow down the results.</SheetDescription>
    </SheetHeader>
    …
    <SheetFooter>
      <SheetClose render={<Button />}>Apply</SheetClose>
    </SheetFooter>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>
```

## Variants

| Prop | Options | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | `top` · `bottom` · `left` · `right` | `right` |

## Parts

- `SheetTrigger` — Opens the Sheet. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button the trigger.
- `SheetClose` — Closes the Sheet. Pass `render={<Button />}` to make your own Button close it.
- `type SheetContentProps`
- `SheetContent` — The panel. `side`: `top` | `right` (default) | `bottom` | `left`. Renders its own portal, overlay and close (×) button.
- `SheetHeader` — Stacks SheetTitle and SheetDescription.
- `SheetFooter` — Action area pinned to the bottom of the panel.
- `SheetTitle` — Required: names the sheet for screen readers.
- `SheetDescription` — Muted text under SheetTitle.

# Sidebar

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { useSidebar, SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarSwitcher, SidebarSwitcherItem, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarSection, SidebarSeparator, SidebarItem, SidebarCategory, SidebarTrigger, type SidebarProviderProps, type SidebarProps, type SidebarSwitcherProps, type SidebarSwitcherItemProps, type SidebarContentProps, type SidebarItemProps, type SidebarCategoryProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

The app's side navigation: a header, the navigation itself (SidebarContent)
and a footer. The navigation is a Tree, and looks like one: folders
(SidebarCategory) with the chevron on the left fold their pages
(SidebarItem) in and out, to any depth, one indent step per level. Tab
visits every visible row, as it does the links of any menu; ↑ ↓ move too,
→ / ← open and close a folder, Enter follows a link or folds a folder,
typing a letter jumps. Items are real links — pass `href`, or `render={<Link href="…" />}`
for your router — and `active` marks the current page. `collapsed` shrinks
it to an icon rail with the labels in tooltips; SidebarTrigger toggles that,
from the SidebarHeader or, under a SidebarProvider, from anywhere on the page.
On small screens render the same content inside a Sheet (`side="left"`).

## Example

```tsx
<Sidebar>
  <SidebarHeader>
    <span className="font-semibold">Torun HR</span>
    <SidebarTrigger />
  </SidebarHeader>
  <SidebarContent aria-label="Main" defaultOpenItems={['time-off']}>
    <SidebarSection title="Workforce">
      <SidebarItem icon={<UsersIcon />} active count={64} render={<Link href="/people" />}>People</SidebarItem>
      <SidebarCategory value="time-off" icon={<CalendarIcon />} label="Time off">
        <SidebarItem render={<Link href="/time-off/requests" />}>Requests</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarCategory value="policies" label="Policies">
          <SidebarItem render={<Link href="/time-off/policies/annual" />}>Annual leave</SidebarItem>
        </SidebarCategory>
      </SidebarCategory>
    </SidebarSection>
  </SidebarContent>
  <SidebarFooter>…</SidebarFooter>
</Sidebar>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `SidebarContextValue`

- `provided: boolean` — Set by SidebarProvider and Sidebar; false only for the default value.

### `CollapsedState`

- `collapsed?: boolean` — Icon rail: icons only, labels in tooltips.

### `SidebarSwitcherProps`

- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — The current choice's logo or icon; decorative, `label` names it. Shown alone on the rail.
- `label: React.ReactNode` — The current choice's name.
- `description?: React.ReactNode` — A quieter second line under the name: a plan, your role there.
- `value?: string` — The `value` of the current SidebarSwitcherItem; it gets the check.

### `SidebarSwitcherItemProps`

- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Its logo or icon, in a small square before the name.

### `SidebarContentProps`

- `'aria-label'?: string` — Names the navigation landmark and its tree. Defaults to "Main".

### `SidebarItemProps`

- `value?: string` — Unique within the sidebar. Defaults to `href`, else a generated id.
- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Optional. Shown before the label, and alone on the rail — so give top-level items one; deeper levels usually go without.
- `active?: boolean` — The current page: a soft brand fill with brand text and icon, `aria-current="page"`.
- `count?: React.ReactNode` — A number or Badge at the end of the row; hidden on the rail.
- `render?: React.ReactElement` — Your router's link, e.g. `<Link href="/people" />`.

### `SidebarCategoryProps`

- `value: string` — Unique within the sidebar; what SidebarContent's open items speak in.
- `icon?: React.ReactNode` — Optional. Shown after the chevron, and alone on the rail — so give top-level categories one.
- `active?: boolean` — One of its pages is current: the category reads as active while closed or on the rail.

## Parts

- `useSidebar` — Whether the surrounding Sidebar (or SidebarProvider) is collapsed to its icon rail, and a setter.
- `type SidebarProviderProps`
- `SidebarProvider` — Holds the Sidebar's collapsed state above it, so a SidebarTrigger can sit outside the sidebar — in the page's top bar, beside the breadcrumb. Renders no element of its own. A Sidebar inside it follows it; give that Sidebar its own `collapsed` (e.g. `collapsed={false}` for the copy in a mobile Sheet) to opt out.

  ```tsx
  <SidebarProvider defaultCollapsed={cookie === '1'} onCollapsedChange={saveCookie}>
    <div className="flex min-h-dvh">
      <Sidebar>…</Sidebar>
      <div className="flex-1">
        <header className="flex h-14 items-center gap-2 px-4">
          <SidebarTrigger className="-ms-2" />
          <Breadcrumb>…</Breadcrumb>
        </header>
        <main>…</main>
      </div>
    </div>
  </SidebarProvider>
  ```

- `type SidebarProps`
- `SidebarHeader` — Top row: the product name or logo, or a SidebarSwitcher, and usually SidebarTrigger. On the rail only the switcher's mark and the trigger show.
- `type SidebarSwitcherProps`
- `SidebarSwitcher` — Switches what the whole app is looking at — a company, a branch, a workspace — from the top of the sidebar: the current one's logo, name and a second line, opening a menu of the others. Put it in SidebarHeader; on the rail it shrinks to the logo. Children are the menu: SidebarSwitcherItems, plus any DropdownMenu parts (a DropdownMenuLabel, a separator, an "Add company" DropdownMenuItem). The app owns what switching means: change `value` (and `label`, `icon`) in `onValueChange`.

  ```tsx
  <SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarSwitcher icon={<img src={org.logo} alt="" />} label={org.name} description="Owner" value={org.id} onValueChange={switchOrg}>
      <DropdownMenuLabel>Companies</DropdownMenuLabel>
      {orgs.map((o) => (
        <SidebarSwitcherItem key={o.id} value={o.id} icon={<img src={o.logo} alt="" />}>{o.name}</SidebarSwitcherItem>
      ))}
      <DropdownMenuSeparator />
      <DropdownMenuItem onClick={addOrg}><PlusIcon />Add company</DropdownMenuItem>
    </SidebarSwitcher>
    <SidebarTrigger />
  </SidebarHeader>
  ```

- `type SidebarSwitcherItemProps`
- `SidebarSwitcherItem` — One choice in a SidebarSwitcher's menu: its logo, its name, and a check on the current one. Picking it closes the menu.
- `type SidebarContentProps`
- `SidebarContent` — The navigation: a `<nav>` landmark around a Tree of SidebarSections, SidebarItems and SidebarCategories. Scrolls when it is taller than the sidebar. Which categories are open is Tree state: `defaultOpenItems` or `openItems` + `onOpenItemsChange`, by category `value`.
- `SidebarFooter` — Bottom row: the signed-in user, a help link. Not part of the navigation tree.
- `SidebarSection` — A group of items under an optional small heading. The heading hides on the rail but still names the group.
- `SidebarSeparator` — Hairline between sections.
- `type SidebarItemProps`
- `SidebarItem` — One page: a link row in the navigation tree. At any level — inside a SidebarCategory it indents one step and lines up under the category's icon.
- `type SidebarCategoryProps`
- `SidebarCategory` — A folder of pages: a branch row with the chevron on the left that folds its SidebarItems — and further SidebarCategories, to any depth — in and out. On the rail, clicking it expands the sidebar and opens it.
- `SidebarTrigger` — Collapses the sidebar to its icon rail and back. Inside the SidebarHeader it sits at the end; under a SidebarProvider it works anywhere, e.g. at the start of the page's top bar.

---

# Skeleton

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading. Give it the size
of the real content with `className`. A brand-blue glint crosses every
skeleton on the page at once, corner to corner and back, so a loading page
reads as one surface; with reduced motion it is a still fill.

## Example

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" />
</div>
```

---

# Spinner

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Spinner, type SpinnerProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Indeterminate loading indicator; `size-4`, inherits text colour. Drawn
inline rather than pulled from an icon set, so the package still pins no icon
library on consumers. A client component: its default name follows the
page's language, which an `aria-label` can only read on the client.

## Example

```tsx
<Button disabled>
  <Spinner label={null} /> Saving…
</Button>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `label?: string | null` — Announced to screen readers; pass null to keep the spinner silent. Defaults to "Loading" in the page's language (see LocaleProvider).

## Parts

- `type SpinnerProps`

---

# SplitButton

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { SplitButton, SplitButtonAction, SplitButtonMenu } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A button with a main action and a menu of related ones: the left half runs
the action, the chevron on the right opens the menu, which opens under the
whole button from its left edge. Two separate buttons, so
each is a tab stop with its own name. `variant` and `size` apply to both halves.

## Example

```tsx
<SplitButton>
  <SplitButtonAction onClick={save}>Save</SplitButtonAction>
  <SplitButtonMenu label="More save options">
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={saveAsDraft}>Save as draft</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={saveAndClose}>Save and close</DropdownMenuItem>
  </SplitButtonMenu>
</SplitButton>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `root: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> | null` — The whole split button, which the menu lines up with.

### `SplitButton`

- `variant?: Variant` — `primary` (default) or `secondary`, for both halves.
- `size?: Size` — `sm` · `md` · `lg`, for both halves.

### `SplitButtonMenu`

- `label: string` — Accessible name of the chevron button.
- `align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'` — Where the menu lines up under the whole split button; its left edge by default.
- `children: React.ReactNode` — The menu's items.

## Parts

- `SplitButtonAction` — The main action, on the left. Disable it alone to leave the menu usable.
- `SplitButtonMenu` — The chevron on the right and the menu it opens; put DropdownMenuItems inside. `label` names the chevron for screen readers ("More save options").

---

# Switch

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Switch, type SwitchProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

On/off toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately. Controlled with
`checked` + `onCheckedChange` (not `onChange`). Renders a native `<button>`,

form, prefer Checkbox.

## Example

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <Switch id="notifications" checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} />
  <Label htmlFor="notifications">Email notifications</Label>
</div>
```

## Parts

- `type SwitchProps`

# Table

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption, exportTable, toXlsxBlob, toCsv, downloadFile, TableCheckbox, tableColumnFilterLabelsForLocale, defaultTableColumnFilterLabels, columnFilterTriggerClass, ColumnFilterPopover, TextFilterPanel, OptionsFilterPanel, NumberFilterPanel, DateFilterPanel, TableColumnFilter, TableColumnOptionsFilter, TableColumnNumberFilter, TableColumnDateFilter, tablePaginationLabelsForLocale, defaultTablePaginationLabels, TablePagination, type TableProps, type TableExportFormat, type TableExportColumn, type TableExportOptions, type TableCheckboxProps, type TableColumnFilterLabels, type TableColumnFilterOption, type TableColumnNumberRange, type TableColumnDateRange, type TableColumnFilterProps, type TableColumnOptionsFilterProps, type TableColumnNumberFilterProps, type TableColumnDateFilterProps, type TablePageSize, type TablePaginationLabels, type TablePaginationProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Plain styled table primitives — no data library, server-renderable; wraps the
table in a horizontally scrolling container. For sorting/pagination over a
column model, use `turkishcoffee/data-table`.

## Example

```tsx
<Table>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
      <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {invoices.map((inv) => (
      <TableRow key={inv.id}>
        <TableCell>{inv.id}</TableCell>
        <TableCell className="text-right">{inv.amount}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `TableProps`

- `containerProps?: React.ComponentProps<'div'>` — Props and ref for the scrolling wrapper; className and ref on Table still target the native table.
- `selectionColor?: TableRowAppearance['selectionColor']` — The background of rows with `data-state="selected"`: `'neutral'` (default) is grey, `'primary'` the brand's soft tint.
- `striped?: boolean` — Alternate the body rows' background. Off by default.

### `TableExportColumn`

- `width?: number` — On-screen width in px; becomes the .xlsx column width.

### `TableExportOptions`

- `fileName?: string` — Without extension. Defaults to "export".
- `locale?: string` — Formats dates and numbers in CSV and picks its delimiter. Defaults to `<html lang>`.

### `TableCheckboxProps`

- `appearance?: 'always' | 'hover'` — `always` (default): visible on every row. `hover`: subtle selection, for dense lists — hidden until its row (`group/row`) or header (`group/header`) is hovered or focused, and shown for good once it is checked, or anything in the table is: pass `revealed`, or put `data-has-selection` on an ancestor (DataTable does, so no row has to re-render).
- `revealed?: boolean` — Keeps a `hover` checkbox visible, e.g. while any row is selected.
- `scope?: 'visible' | 'all'` — For a checked header box: `'all'` (default) — every row is selected, a filled box. `'visible'` — only the rows on screen (this page) are; an outlined box, so it reads differently from "everything". The usual two-step: first click selects the page, the next one everything.

### `TableColumnFilterLabels`

- `filter: (column: string) => string` — Title and trigger name: "Filter Name".
- `contains: string` — Caption above the text filter's input.
- `searchOptions: string` — The options filter's search field, shown from six options.
- `noOptions: string` — The options filter when its search matches none.
- `min: string` — The number filter's lower bound.
- `max: string` — The number filter's upper bound.
- `pickDates: string` — The date filter before a day is picked.

### `TableColumnFilterOption`

- `count?: number` — Shown beside the label: the rows with this value, when the app knows.

### `TableColumnFilterProps`

- `column: string` — The column's name, for the title and the trigger's accessible name.
- `value: string` — The applied filter text; empty when none.
- `onApply: (value: string) => void` — Called with the new text, or `''` to clear.
- `tabIndex?: number` — The funnel's tab order; a grid that manages focus itself passes -1.

### `TableColumnOptionsFilterProps`

- `column: string` — The column's name, for the title and the trigger's accessible name.
- `value: readonly unknown[] | undefined` — The values shown; `undefined` when nothing is filtered out.
- `onApply: (value: Array<TableColumnFilterOption['value']> | undefined) => void` — The ticked values, or `undefined` when none is ticked.
- `locale?: string` — Formats the counts and folds case for the search; the page's language.
- `tabIndex?: number` — The funnel's tab order; a grid that manages focus itself passes -1.

### `TableColumnNumberFilterProps`

- `column: string` — The column's name, for the title and the trigger's accessible name.
- `onApply: (value: TableColumnNumberRange | undefined) => void` — The bounds, or `undefined` when both are empty.
- `tabIndex?: number` — The funnel's tab order; a grid that manages focus itself passes -1.

### `TableColumnDateFilterProps`

- `column: string` — The column's name, for the title and the trigger's accessible name.
- `onApply: (value: TableColumnDateRange | undefined) => void` — The days picked (`from` and `to` the same for one day), or `undefined` to clear.
- `locale?: string` — Month and day names, the first day of the week and the summary's format.
- `tabIndex?: number` — The funnel's tab order; a grid that manages focus itself passes -1.

### `TablePaginationLabels`

- `range: (from: number, to: number, total: number) => string` — "1–10 of 1374". `from` is 0 when there are no rows.

### `TablePaginationProps`

- `page: number` — The current page, 1-based.
- `total: number` — Rows across all pages.
- `pageSizeOptions?: TablePageSize[]` — Choices in the page-size picker. Defaults to 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 and All.
- `onPageSizeChange?: (pageSize: TablePageSize) => void` — Omit to hide the page-size picker.
- `locale?: string` — The labels' language and numerals. Defaults to LocaleProvider's, else the page's `<html lang>`.
- `disabled?: boolean` — Disables every control, e.g. while the next page is loading.

## Parts

- `type TableProps`
- `TableHeader` — The `<thead>`.
- `TableBody` — The `<tbody>`.
- `TableFooter` — The `<tfoot>`, e.g. for totals.
- `TableRow` — A `<tr>`; in a `striped` Table body rows alternate between `--table-row-odd` and `--table-row-even`. Headers and footers keep their own background. Highlights on hover and when `data-state="selected"`.
- `TableHead` — A header cell (`<th>`).
- `TableCell` — A body cell (`<td>`). Does not wrap by default (`whitespace-nowrap`).
- `TableCaption` — The `<caption>`, rendered below the table.
- `type TableExportFormat` — What a table export writes.
- `type TableExportColumn` — One exported column: its heading, how to read a row's value, and optionally its width in px.
- `type TableExportOptions`
- `exportTable` — Downloads rows as a CSV or Excel file. Data-agnostic: pass the columns and rows to write, in order — DataTable's `getExportData` hands over exactly that. Values keep their type: numbers, dates and booleans are real Excel numbers, dates and booleans in .xlsx. The .xlsx writer (`write-excel-file`) is imported on first use: pages that never export to Excel never download it.

  ```tsx
  await exportTable({
    format: 'xlsx',
    fileName: 'employees',
    columns: [
      { label: 'Name', value: (e) => e.name },
      { label: 'Start date', value: (e) => e.startDate },
    ],
    rows: employees,
  })
  ```

- `toXlsxBlob` — The .xlsx workbook for `exportTable`, as a Blob — to upload or attach instead of downloading. A bold, frozen header row; numbers, dates and booleans as real Excel values; dates in the locale's short format. Loads the writer on first use.
- `toCsv` — The CSV text for `exportTable`: a UTF-8 BOM so Excel reads Turkish letters, and `;` between fields where the locale writes decimals with a comma (Turkish Excel expects that), `,` elsewhere.
- `downloadFile` — Saves a blob as a file through a temporary link.
- `type TableCheckboxProps`
- `TableCheckbox` — The selection checkbox of a table row or header. A header box shows the mixed state with `indeterminate`, and "this page only" with `scope="visible"`. Give every box an `aria-label`.

  ```tsx
  <TableRow data-state={selected ? 'selected' : undefined} className="group/row">
    <TableCell>
      <TableCheckbox appearance="hover" checked={selected} onCheckedChange={setSelected} aria-label="Select row" />
    </TableCell>
  </TableRow>
  ```

- `type TableColumnFilterLabels` — Every word the column filters render, in the locale's language (see LocaleProvider).
- `tableColumnFilterLabelsForLocale` — The labels in `locale`'s language.
- `defaultTableColumnFilterLabels` — The English labels.
- `columnFilterTriggerClass` — The funnel: hidden until its header (`group/header`) is hovered or focused, and visible, filled, in the brand colour, while a filter is applied.
- `ColumnFilterPopover` — The funnel and its panel, shared by every column filter. The panel is as wide as its content needs (translated buttons, a calendar) and never narrower than 16rem, so nothing in it runs past its edge. `children` renders only while the panel is open, so each opening starts from the applied value.
- `TextFilterPanel` — The "contains" panel. Applies the trimmed text, `''` to clear.
- `type TableColumnFilterOption` — One choice of an options filter: the value matched, its label, and how many rows hold it.
- `OptionsFilterPanel` — The checklist panel: tick the values to show. Nothing ticked is no filter, so there is no "Select all" to keep in step. From six options a search field above narrows the list; ArrowDown moves from it into the list.
- `type TableColumnNumberRange` — A number filter's value: the inclusive bounds, either of which may be missing.
- `NumberFilterPanel` — Min and Max side by side. Either may stay empty; reversed bounds are swapped.
- `type TableColumnDateRange` — A date filter's value: whole days, both ends included; either may be missing.
- `DateFilterPanel` — A calendar to pick one day (click it once) or a range (click both ends). Month and year are drop-downs, to reach years back quickly. Month and day names follow `locale`.
- `type TableColumnFilterProps`
- `TableColumnFilter` — A column header's "contains" filter: a funnel that opens a small panel with a text field and Apply / Clear / Cancel. Enter applies, Escape cancels. The funnel stays hidden until its header (`group/header`) is hovered or focused, and stays visible — filled — while a filter is applied. Controlled: the caller owns the applied value and does the filtering.

  ```tsx
  <TableHead className="group/header">
    Name
    <TableColumnFilter column="Name" value={nameFilter} onApply={setNameFilter} />
  </TableHead>
  ```

- `type TableColumnOptionsFilterProps`
- `TableColumnOptionsFilter` — A column header's filter for a column of known values (a status, a type, a department): the same funnel as TableColumnFilter, opening a checklist with each option's count beside it, and Apply / Clear / Cancel. Tick the values to show; with none ticked nothing is filtered. From six options a search field above the list narrows it. Controlled: the caller owns the applied values and does the filtering.

  ```tsx
  <TableColumnOptionsFilter
    column="Status"
    options={[{ value: 'active', label: 'Active', count: 12 }, { value: 'passive', label: 'Passive', count: 3 }]}
    value={statuses}
    onApply={setStatuses}
  />
  ```

- `type TableColumnNumberFilterProps`
- `TableColumnNumberFilter` — A column header's filter for numbers: Min and Max, both inclusive, either optional. Same funnel and actions as TableColumnFilter. Controlled.

  ```tsx
  <TableColumnNumberFilter column="Salary" value={salary} onApply={setSalary} />
  ```

- `type TableColumnDateFilterProps`
- `TableColumnDateFilter` — A column header's filter for dates: a calendar picking one day or a range, both ends included. Same funnel and actions as TableColumnFilter. Controlled.

  ```tsx
  <TableColumnDateFilter column="Start date" value={started} onApply={setStarted} locale="tr-TR" />
  ```

- `type TablePageSize` — A page size, or every row on one page.
- `type TablePaginationLabels` — Every word TablePagination renders, in the locale's language (see LocaleProvider).
- `tablePaginationLabelsForLocale` — The labels in `locale`'s language, with its numerals.
- `defaultTablePaginationLabels` — The English labels.
- `type TablePaginationProps`
- `TablePagination` — The bar under a table: rows per page, the visible range, and first/previous/next/last buttons. Controlled and data-agnostic, so it pages a server-driven list as well as DataTable's client rows (which renders it for you).

  ```tsx
  <TablePagination
    page={page}
    pageSize={pageSize}
    total={1374}
    onPageChange={setPage}
    onPageSizeChange={(size) => { setPageSize(size); setPage(1) }}
  />
  ```

---

# Tabs

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Switches between views in the same place. Uncontrolled with `defaultValue`,
controlled with `value` + `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)`.

## Example

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="account">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="password">Password</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="account">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="password">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

## Parts

- `TabsList` — The row of TabsTriggers.
- `TabsTrigger` — Selects the TabsContent with the same `value`.
- `TabsContent` — Panel shown while its `value` is selected.

---

# Textarea

**Server-renderable**: no `"use client"`; it adds no client boundary.

```tsx
import { Textarea, type TextareaProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Multi-line text field; grows with its content (`field-sizing-content`) from a
minimum of `min-h-16`. Server-renderable.

## Example

```tsx
<Textarea placeholder="Leave a comment" rows={4} />
```

## Parts

- `type TextareaProps`

---

# Toast

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { toast, useSonner, Toaster, type ExternalToast, type ToasterProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Mount once, near the root of the app. Then call `toast()` from anywhere.
Renders through a portal, so placement in the tree does not matter.

Colors come from the theme tokens, so it follows `.dark` without a `theme` prop.
Pass `richColors` to render `toast.success` / `toast.error` in solid token colors.

`toast.success`, `toast.error` and `toast.info` carry the library's filled
SuccessIcon, ErrorIcon and InfoIcon; `toast.warning` shares ErrorIcon in the
warning colour. Override any of them with the `icons` prop (`null` removes one).

A plain `toast()` is white on the `--inverse` grey, the same surface Tooltip
uses; its action button sits on that grey with a lighter outline.

## Example

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
<body>
  {children}
  <Toaster />
</body>

// anywhere in a client component
toast.success('Saved', { description: 'Your changes are live.' })
```

## Parts

- `toast` — Re-exported from sonner: `toast()` plus `toast.success`, `.error`, `.promise`, `.dismiss`.
- `useSonner`
- `type ExternalToast`
- `type ToasterProps`

---

# Tooltip

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { TooltipTrigger, Tooltip, TooltipContent, type TooltipContentProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

Short text hint shown on hover and keyboard focus. Self-providing: no need
to wrap your app in a TooltipProvider (there is none to import). `delay` is
the hover delay in ms (200 by default). Not shown on touch devices — never put
essential information in it.

## Example

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Copy" />}>
    <CopyIcon />
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Copy to clipboard</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

- `delay?: number` — Hover delay before the tooltip opens, in ms.

## Parts

- `TooltipTrigger` — The element the Tooltip describes. Pass `render={<Button />}` to use a Button.
- `type TooltipContentProps`
- `TooltipContent` — The hint bubble; renders its own portal and arrow.

---

# Tree

**Client component** (`"use client"`): import it from server components too. It renders to HTML on the server, then hydrates in the browser for its interactivity.

```tsx
import { Tree, TreeItem, TreeGroup, useTreeItem, TreeItemRow, TreeItemLayout, TreeItemPersonaLayout, type TreeProps, type TreeItemProps, type TreeItemRowProps, type TreeItemLayoutProps, type TreeItemPersonaLayoutProps } from 'turkishcoffee'
```

A hierarchy people expand and collapse: folders and files, an org chart,
nested categories, an app's navigation (Sidebar is built on it). Build it
from TreeItems; a branch holds its children in a TreeGroup. One tab stop
(or one per row with `tabStops="every"`): ↑ ↓ move, → opens a branch or enters it, ← closes it or goes to the parent,
Home / End jump, `*` opens every sibling, and typing a letter jumps to the
next item starting with it. Branches open on click and Enter; `onAction`
fires for every item. Rows are TreeItemLayout, TreeItemPersonaLayout or your
own built on TreeItemRow. Name the tree with `aria-label`.

## Example

```tsx
<Tree aria-label="Files" defaultOpenItems={['docs']} selectionMode="single">
  <TreeItem value="docs" itemType="branch">
    <TreeItemLayout iconBefore={<FolderIcon />} aside={<Badge>2</Badge>}>Documents</TreeItemLayout>
    <TreeGroup>
      <TreeItem value="contract">
        <TreeItemLayout iconBefore={<FileIcon />}>Contract.pdf</TreeItemLayout>
      </TreeItem>
    </TreeGroup>
  </TreeItem>
</Tree>
```

## Props

Only props this library adds or changes; everything else forwards to the underlying element or Base UI part.

### `TreeProps`

- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` — Row height: `sm` 24px or `md` 32px (default).
- `selectionMode?: SelectionMode` — `none` (default) · `single` · `multiple` (with checkboxes). Selection never cascades to children.
- `openItems?: string[]` — Values of the open branches.
- `selectedItems?: string[]` — Values of the selected items.
- `onAction?: (value: string) => void` — Called when an item is clicked or activated with Enter: open a file, navigate to a page.
- `tabStops?: 'one' | 'every'` — `one` (default): the tree is one tab stop and arrow keys move inside it, the ARIA tree pattern, right for a file tree with hundreds of rows. `every`: each visible row is a tab stop too, as links in a navigation menu are; the arrow keys still work. Rows of closed branches are not rendered, so Tab never lands in them.

### `TreeItemProps`

- `value: string` — Unique within the Tree; what openItems, selectedItems and onAction speak in.
- `itemType?: 'branch' | 'leaf'` — `branch` holds a TreeGroup and opens; `leaf` (default) does not.

### `TreeItemLayoutProps`

- `iconBefore?: React.ReactNode` — Icon before the text, e.g. a folder.
- `iconAfter?: React.ReactNode` — Icon after the text, e.g. a lock.
- `aside?: React.ReactNode` — Quiet content at the end of the row: a count, a Badge, a date. Hidden while `actions` show.
- `actions?: React.ReactNode` — Buttons shown on hover and focus, e.g. a "More" menu: ghost `size="icon"` Buttons (sized to the row).

### `TreeItemPersonaLayoutProps`

- `media: React.ReactNode` — An Avatar (sized `size-8`, or `size-6` in a `sm` tree).
- `description?: React.ReactNode` — The second line: a title, an email, a status.

## Parts

- `type TreeProps`
- `type TreeItemProps`
- `TreeItem` — One node. Put a row in it (TreeItemLayout, TreeItemPersonaLayout or your own TreeItemRow) and, for a branch, a TreeGroup after it.
- `TreeGroup` — A branch's children. Rendered only while the branch is open.
- `useTreeItem` — The state of the TreeItem around you, for building your own row: its level, whether it is a branch and open, whether it is selected, and setters.
- `type TreeItemRowProps`
- `TreeItemRow` — The focusable row of a TreeItem — the element that is the `treeitem`. It carries the tree's roles, focus and click behaviour and nothing visual: build your own row on it, or render it as a link with `render={<a href="…" />}`. Clicking it opens a branch, selects, and fires `onAction`; call `event.preventDefault()` in your `onClick` to skip that.
- `type TreeItemLayoutProps`
- `TreeItemLayout` — The standard row: chevron, optional icon, text, then `aside` (quiet) or `actions` (on hover and focus). Indents itself by level; fixed height.
- `type TreeItemPersonaLayoutProps`
- `TreeItemPersonaLayout` — A person row: avatar, name and a second line. For org charts and team pickers.
